fact: Claude Console is Anthropic's console at platform.claude.com, where Claude Console organizations hold API workloads (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/admin-api-keys)

Anthropic has two separate tenancy models: Claude Console organizations managed at platform.claude.com and Claude Enterprise organizations managed at claude.ai, and a company using both creates admin keys in each (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/admin-api-keys)

A Claude Enterprise tenant has one parent organization that centralizes identity, with linked claude.ai organizations (chat and content) and linked Claude Console organizations (API workloads); a standalone Console organization has no parent (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/compliance-api)

The Claude Console hierarchy is organization > workspaces; workspaces (IDs prefixed wrkspc_) hold members, service accounts, API keys and limits (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workspaces)
Every Claude Console organization has a Default Workspace that cannot be renamed, archived or deleted (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workspaces)
The default cap is 100 workspaces per Claude Console organization (archived ones excluded), raisable via the account team (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workspaces)

Only Claude Console organization admins can create workspaces, and organization users and developers must be added to workspaces by an admin (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workspaces)

Claude Console workspaces can be created in the Console at platform.claude.com/settings/workspaces or via the Admin API at /v1/organizations/workspaces (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workspaces)

When a member first signs in to Claude Code with a Console account, Anthropic creates a Claude Code workspace, mints a per-user key there (keys cannot be created manually in it) and rate-limits it separately; it is the only workspace supporting per-user monthly spend limits (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workspaces)
Archiving the Claude Code workspace disables Claude Code sign-in through Console billing (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workspaces)

The Claude Admin API is available to Claude Console and Claude Enterprise organizations but not to claude.ai Team plan organizations or individual Console accounts (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/admin-api)
Individual Console accounts must set up an organization at platform.claude.com/settings/organization before using the Admin API (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/admin-api)

Signing up for Claude Platform on AWS via the AWS Console creates a new Anthropic organization bound to the AWS account, and the AWS Console checks for and prompts acceptance of any private offer (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws ; https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing)

Existing first-party Anthropic organizations cannot be converted to Claude Platform on AWS, and their keys and settings do not carry over (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws)
Claude Platform on AWS launched on 2026-05-11 (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/release-notes/overview)

Claude in Microsoft Foundry is provisioned as a Foundry resource in an Azure subscription that holds security and billing configuration, with Claude deployments inside it as the callable model instances (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry)
The first Claude deployment in Microsoft Foundry requires accepting Azure Marketplace terms (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry)

Amazon Bedrock access to Claude requires a one-time Anthropic use case form per AWS account, submitted from the Bedrock Model catalog (access granted immediately) or once from the AWS Organizations management account via PutUseCaseForModelAccess, which extends to child accounts (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/amazon-bedrock)

Submitting the Anthropic use case form from the AWS Organizations management account uses PutUseCaseForModelAccess and needs the bedrock:PutUseCaseForModelAccess permission (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/amazon-bedrock)

Bedrock sets access criteria per Claude model: on the bedrock-mantle endpoint Claude Fable 5.1, Fable 5, Opus 4.8, Sonnet 5, Opus 4.7 and Haiku 4.5 are open to all Bedrock customers, and other models' criteria are shown in Bedrock model access (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-amazon-bedrock)
Claude Mythos models on Amazon Bedrock require verification before access (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-amazon-bedrock)
Claude Enterprise is obtained via Anthropic sales (https://claude.com/pricing ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/iam)
Claude Team is a self-service plan for 2 to 150 seats (https://claude.com/pricing ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/iam)

Day-one asks for an engineer joining a client engagement: which surface the client uses (Claude API direct, Claude Platform on AWS, Bedrock, Google Cloud Anthropic-managed or Google-managed, Foundry), the organization ID and target wrkspc_ workspace ID, a service account (svac_...) or federation rule (fdrl_...) created by an org admin or a workspace-scoped personal key, workspace rate and spend limits, and whether ZDR, HIPAA readiness or IP allowlisting are enabled (secondary: synthesis of cited docs) (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/authentication ; https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workload-identity-federation)
The Claude API accepts static API keys (sk-ant-api...) sent as Authorization: Bearer or legacy x-api-key (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/authentication)
The Claude API accepts Workload Identity Federation, short-lived tokens exchanged from an IdP token (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/authentication)

The Claude API accepts App Attest for iOS/macOS apps, issuing 1-hour tokens scoped to a workspace that work with the Messages API only (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/authentication)
A Claude personal API key acts as the user and stops working when the user leaves (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/authentication)
A Claude service account key acts as a service account (svac_...) and stops working when the service account is archived (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/authentication)
A Claude workspace key belongs to no identity and is legacy; Anthropic recommends identity-backed keys or WIF for new integrations (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/authentication)
Claude personal and service account keys have been available since 2026-08-27 (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/release-notes/overview)

Personal and service account keys can be scoped to one workspace or to all workspaces the identity can access; a key not scoped to a workspace must send the anthropic-workspace-id header on every request or the API returns 400 invalid_request_error, and an inaccessible workspace returns 404 (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/authentication)
Claude API keys are created only in the Console, not via the Admin API; the Admin API can only list, rename and change the status of keys (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/admin-api)

Each key listed by the Admin API reports expires_at, principal (user_actor, service_account_actor or null for workspace keys) and scope (workspace or organization) (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/admin-api)

Claude API key expiration is set at creation and cannot be changed, with presets of 3 hours, 1 day, 7 days, 30 days, custom or Never; an organization maximum-expiration policy removes Never; expired keys return 401 authentication_error and cannot be reactivated; available since 2026-07-08 (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/authentication ; https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/release-notes/overview)

With Claude Workload Identity Federation, workloads exchange an IdP-issued JWT at POST /v1/oauth/token (RFC 7523 jwt-bearer grant) for a short-lived sk-ant-oat01-... token acting as a service account (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workload-identity-federation)

Claude Workload Identity Federation supports IdPs including AWS IAM, Google Cloud, Microsoft Entra ID, GitHub Actions, Kubernetes, SPIFFE, Okta and any OIDC issuer (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workload-identity-federation)
Claude Workload Identity Federation launched on 2026-05-04 (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/release-notes/overview)
Claude WIF uses federation issuers (fdis_...) to register an OIDC provider (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workload-identity-federation)

Claude WIF federation rules (fdrl_...) match JWT claims (subject_prefix, audience, claims map, or CEL condition) to a target service account and an OAuth scope (default workspace:developer) (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workload-identity-federation)

Setting up Claude WIF requires the admin, owner or primary owner role, via the Console Connect workload wizard at platform.claude.com/settings/workload-identity-federation (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workload-identity-federation)

Claude WIF token lifetime is 60 to 86,400 seconds (default 3,600); the minted lifetime is the lesser of the rule's token_lifetime_seconds and twice the IdP JWT's remaining lifetime (minimum 60 s), the Console wizard prefills 600 s, and JWTs with a jti are single-use by default (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workload-identity-federation)

Anthropic SDKs use WIF when ANTHROPIC_FEDERATION_RULE_ID, ANTHROPIC_ORGANIZATION_ID, ANTHROPIC_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_ID, ANTHROPIC_WORKSPACE_ID and ANTHROPIC_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE are set (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workload-identity-federation)
A leftover ANTHROPIC_API_KEY outranks federation in SDK credential precedence and silently overrides WIF (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workload-identity-federation)
ant auth status reports which credential won in Anthropic credential precedence (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workload-identity-federation)

A Claude service account (svac_...) is a non-human identity with no email, password or Console login, implicitly a member of the Default Workspace and added to other workspaces explicitly (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workload-identity-federation)

No separate agent identity type was found in the Anthropic docs; service accounts are the closest thing to an agent identity (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workload-identity-federation)

The Claude Admin API accepts an Admin API key (sk-ant-admin...), created only by organization admins, or a personal/service account key that is not workspace-scoped (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/admin-api)
The Claude Admin API accepts an OAuth bearer token with org:admin scope (admin, owner or primary owner) (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/admin-api)
ant auth login --profile admin --scope "org:admin" obtains an org:admin OAuth token for the Claude Admin API (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/admin-api)
The Admin API's service-account, federation-issuer and federation-rule endpoints accept only org:admin OAuth tokens (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/admin-api)
Claude Enterprise Admin API keys are created at claude.ai > Organization settings > API with prefix sk-ant-api01- (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/admin-api-keys)

The primary owner can grant any scope on a Claude Enterprise Admin API key, while organization owners can grant only Compliance API scopes (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/admin-api-keys)

Claude Enterprise Admin API key scopes include read:members, write:members, read:rbac_groups, write:rbac_groups, read:plugins, write:plugins, read:claude_tag, write:claude_tag, read:spend_limits, write:spend_limits, read:analytics, read:compliance_activities, read:compliance_user_data, delete:compliance_user_data, read:compliance_org_data and read:org_audit (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/admin-api-keys)
Human SSO for Claude Team, Enterprise and Console organizations supports SAML (https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13132885-setting-up-single-sign-on-sso)
Human SSO for Claude Team, Enterprise and Console organizations supports OIDC (https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13132885-setting-up-single-sign-on-sso)

Claude SSO domains are verified with a DNS TXT record (all from one IdP); setup guides cover Okta, Entra ID, Google Workspace, OneLogin, JumpCloud, Duo and Ping, and admins can toggle Require SSO for Claude and Require SSO for Console (article updated 2026-10-13) (https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13132885-setting-up-single-sign-on-sso)

Claude Code authentication options are a Claude Pro/Max/Ultra subscription, a Claude for Teams or Enterprise account, Claude Console, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry, Claude Platform on AWS, a self-hosted Claude apps gateway (corporate SSO), Anthropic profiles and WIF credentials (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/iam)
Claude Code can sign in with Claude Console without creating an API key (keyless) since v2.1.242 (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/iam)

Claude Code credential precedence is: cloud provider (CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK / CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX / CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY), ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, apiKeyHelper output, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, Anthropic profile/federation credentials, then subscription OAuth from /login (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/iam)
claude setup-token mints a one-year CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN for Claude Code (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/iam)

Claude Code stores credentials in the macOS Keychain, in ~/.claude/.credentials.json (mode 0600) on Linux and %USERPROFILE%\.claude\.credentials.json on Windows; Anthropic profiles live in ~/.config/anthropic or %APPDATA%\Anthropic (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/iam)

Admins can force the Claude Code login method and organization with managed settings forceLoginMethod (claudeai, console, gateway) and forceLoginOrgUUID, and allowedProviders (v2.1.285+) restricts which providers a machine may use (e.g. anthropic, bedrock, customEndpoint) (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/iam)

The recommended Amazon Bedrock authentication path for Claude is a Bedrock service role (iam:PassRole); IAM assumed roles via SAML/OIDC/IAM Identity Center are also supported with a 12-hour max session (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-amazon-bedrock ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/amazon-bedrock)

Amazon Bedrock accepts bearer tokens/API keys via AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK, with short-term keys lasting up to 12 hours (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-amazon-bedrock ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/amazon-bedrock)

Admins can deny long-term Bedrock API keys with a bedrock:BearerTokenType condition on bedrock:CallWithBearerToken (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-amazon-bedrock ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/amazon-bedrock)
Claude Platform on AWS authenticates with SigV4 using service name aws-external-anthropic (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws)

The Claude Console organization role user gives playground access (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/admin-api)

The Claude Console workspace role workspace_developer covers keys and API (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workspaces)
The Claude Console Workspace Admin role has full workspace control (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workspaces)
The Claude Console Workspace Billing role is inherited from the org billing role and is not assignable (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workspaces)
Claude Console org admins automatically get Workspace Admin in all workspaces, while org users and developers must be added explicitly (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workspaces)

Least-privilege runtime identity for an agent calling the Claude API: create a dedicated workspace, have an org admin create a service account added only to that workspace, and either issue a service account key scoped to that single workspace with a short expiration or (preferred) bind a WIF federation rule with scope workspace:developer to that workspace, then set workspace RPM/ITPM/OTPM and monthly spend limits below the org limits (secondary: synthesis of cited docs) (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/authentication ; https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workload-identity-federation ; https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workspaces)

Files, Message Batches, Skills and prompt caches are isolated per workspace on the Claude API, Claude Platform on AWS and Foundry, while on Bedrock and Google-managed Google Cloud prompt caches are isolated per organization (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workspaces)
Claude MCP tunnels are managed with a workspace:manage_tunnels OAuth token from WIF (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workspaces)
Claude MCP tunnels are capped at 10 active tunnels per organization, and organization developers can view but not change them (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workspaces)

Workspaces, service accounts, federation issuers/rules and Admin API keys are created by Claude Console org admins (or owners/primary owners) (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workspaces)

IP allowlisting for Claude Console and Enterprise organizations launched in beta on 2026-11-05 (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/ip-allowlist ; https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/release-notes/overview)
Claude IP allowlists are set by org admins/owners (Console) or owners/primary owners (Enterprise) (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/ip-allowlist)
Claude IP allowlisting allows up to 1,000 public IPv4/IPv6 entries (no broader than /8 or /32), and changes take up to 15 minutes (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/ip-allowlist)

Blocked API calls get 403 permission_error; allowlisting covers Messages, Batches, Token Counting, Models, Files, Skills, Managed Agents endpoints, Admin API and Compliance API, but does not apply to Bedrock, Claude Platform on AWS, Google Cloud or Foundry (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/ip-allowlist)

No PrivateLink or private endpoint offering for api.anthropic.com appeared in the docs reviewed; private networking is available through the cloud platforms (unverified for direct API) (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry)
Foundry resources hosting Claude can be added to an Azure Virtual Network (Private Link) (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry)

Claude inference_geo per request is "global" (default) or "us", and workspaces can set allowed_inference_geos and default_inference_geo in the Console or via the Admin API data_residency field (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/data-residency)
Claude workspace geo (storage at rest and endpoint processing) is fixed at workspace creation and only "us" is available (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/data-residency)
Claude data residency settings are supported on Claude 4.6 and later models; earlier models return 400 (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/data-residency)

inference_geo: "us" applies a 1.1x multiplier to all token categories on Claude 4.6+ models on the Claude API, Claude Platform on AWS and Google Cloud (Anthropic managed); Foundry US Data Zone Standard deployments apply the same 1.1x, and rate limits are shared across geos (shown 2026-11-14) (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/data-residency ; https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing)

Organizations that previously opted out of global routing were migrated automatically to allowed_inference_geos: ["us"] and default_inference_geo: "us" (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/data-residency)

Bedrock sets Claude residency by endpoint, not inference_geo, offering global and regional endpoints plus US/EU/JP/AU inference profiles (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-amazon-bedrock)

fact: Google-managed regional endpoints serve only Claude Sonnet 4.6 and earlier (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-models-on-google-cloud/google-managed)

Section B of the Anthropic Commercial Terms of Service (version effective 2025-06-17) states "Anthropic may not train models on Customer Content from Services" (https://www.anthropic.com/legal/commercial-terms)

Inputs and outputs from Claude for Work and the API are not used for training by default, but submitted feedback (thumbs up/down) may be used and is kept up to 5 years (article updated 2026-08-18) (https://privacy.claude.com/en/articles/7996868-is-my-data-used-for-model-training)
Team/Enterprise Primary Owners and Owners can disable member feedback via the Rate chats setting (https://privacy.claude.com/en/articles/7996868-is-my-data-used-for-model-training)

Per the privacy center (updated 2026-07-01), Anthropic automatically deletes API inputs and outputs on its backend within 30 days of receipt or generation, except user-controlled storage (e.g. Files API), ZDR agreements, Usage Policy enforcement and legal requirements; flagged content is kept up to 2 years and classifier scores up to 7 years (https://privacy.claude.com/en/articles/7996866-how-long-do-you-store-my-organization-s-data)

The API data retention doc says prompts and outputs are not retained by default except for Covered Models (30-day retention) and that retained data is never used for training without express permission, which differs from the privacy center's within-30-days wording; its date is not shown (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/api-and-data-retention)
Claude ZDR is a per-organization arrangement obtained through sales, and each new organization must be enabled separately (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/api-and-data-retention)

Under ZDR Anthropic does not store prompts or responses at rest after the response; it covers the Messages and Token Counting APIs for eligible features and Claude Code with Commercial-organization API keys (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/api-and-data-retention)
ZDR organizations cannot call the Claude API from a browser (CORS rejected) (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/api-and-data-retention)

ZDR does not cover Claude Console/playground, Claude Managed Agents (except self-hosted), consumer plans, Team and Enterprise product interfaces (except Claude Code on Enterprise's separate ZDR offering), Claude for Excel, Covered Models or third-party integrations; stateful features such as Agent Skills and code execution are No for ZDR but are not blocked (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/api-and-data-retention)
Claude Managed Agents is not covered by ZDR except self-hosted Managed Agents (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/api-and-data-retention)

Claude Fable 5.2, Mythos 5.2, Fable 5.1, Mythos 5.1, Fable 5 and Mythos 5 require 30-day retention and are not available under ZDR unless Anthropic authorizes it; the Fable 5 rule applies since 2026-06-09 (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/api-and-data-retention ; https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/release-notes/overview)
The 30-day retention rule has applied to the 5.2 models (Fable 5.2, Mythos 5.2) since 2026-11-09 (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/release-notes/overview)
ZDR organizations can enable Standard data retention for a non-default workspace to use Covered Models (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/api-and-data-retention)

Eligible Claude Console org admins enable HIPAA readiness self-serve by accepting Anthropic's standard BAA at platform.claude.com/settings/privacy (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/api-and-data-retention)

Claude HIPAA readiness is enforced org-wide, cannot be disabled once enabled, and the API returns 400 for non-eligible features (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/api-and-data-retention)

Claude HIPAA readiness is not available on Claude Platform on AWS, Bedrock, Google Cloud Agent Platform, or for Claude Code via API; Foundry is eligible with a BAA and Azure HIPAA configuration (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/api-and-data-retention)
Claude Code ZDR is a separate offering available to qualified Claude for Enterprise accounts via sales and enabled per organization (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/zero-data-retention)
Claude Code ZDR disables cloud sessions, Claude Tag, artifacts in Claude Code, Claude Docs, feedback submission and Remote Control (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/zero-data-retention)

Claude Enterprise Primary Owners and Owners set retention for chats, projects and artifacts under Organization settings > Data and Privacy (https://privacy.claude.com/en/articles/10440198-custom-data-retention-controls-for-claude-enterprise)

Claude Enterprise custom data retention has a minimum of 30 days and a default of indefinite retention (https://privacy.claude.com/en/articles/10440198-custom-data-retention-controls-for-claude-enterprise)
Shortening Claude Enterprise data retention is irreversible (https://privacy.claude.com/en/articles/10440198-custom-data-retention-controls-for-claude-enterprise)

Claude Compliance API endpoints are under /v1/compliance/* on api.anthropic.com, including the Activity Feed GET /v1/compliance/activities, retained 6 years (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/compliance-api)
The Compliance API Activity Feed is available to Console Admin API keys and to Enterprise keys with read:compliance_activities (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/compliance-api)

Compliance API content endpoints (chats, files, projects, session transcripts for Cowork, Claude Code, Claude in Chrome, etc.) and directory endpoints require an Enterprise Compliance Access Key (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/compliance-api ; https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/api-and-data-retention)
The Claude Compliance API has a shared limit of 600 requests/minute per parent organization (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/compliance-api)

Owners and primary owners can download a CSV of organization events from claude.ai > Organization settings > Data and privacy, with a capped lookback window and no content, narrower than the Compliance API (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/compliance-api)
Inference hooks provide inline prompt governance on Claude Enterprise (details not reviewed) (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/compliance-api)
Inference hooks send each governed prompt to the organization's AI security server before inference, which can deny it in real time (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/compliance-api)
Owners/Primary Owners (and Enterprise custom roles with Libraries permission) use Organization settings > Plugins & skills to control plugins and skills (https://claude.com/docs/plugins/admin.md)

Claude Plugins & skills settings set availability (Not available, Available to install, Installed by default, Required), sync marketplaces from GitHub/GitLab, and toggle User-created skills, sharing, publishing review and security scanning; connectors are allowed separately in Organization settings > Connectors, and Enterprise supports per-group availability via SCIM-synced groups (https://claude.com/docs/plugins/admin.md)

Claude Code managed settings sources in priority order are server-managed settings (claude.ai admin console or Claude apps gateway, polled hourly), MDM/OS policy (macOS com.anthropic.claudecode profile or Windows HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\ClaudeCode Settings value), managed settings files (C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\managed-settings.json, /Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/, /etc/claude-code/, plus managed-mcp.json), then HKCU; default behavior is first-wins (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/managed-settings)

Claude Code managed policy keys include disableBypassPermissionsMode, allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly, allowManagedMcpServersOnly, allowedMcpServers, deniedMcpServers, disableClaudeAiConnectors and strictKnownMarketplaces (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/managed-settings)

Server-managed Claude Code settings require Team or Enterprise, configured at claude.ai Organization settings > Claude Code > Managed settings; Enterprise can give groups different settings (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/server-managed-settings)
Configuring server-managed Claude Code settings requires the Owner or Primary Owner role (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/server-managed-settings)

Only sessions authenticating to Anthropic with an eligible credential fetch server-managed settings, so they do not apply to Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry sessions (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/server-managed-settings ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/managed-settings)

Cloud platform logging is the customer's responsibility: Bedrock emits CloudWatch and CloudTrail logs, and Anthropic recommends keeping at least 30 days of logs (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-amazon-bedrock)

Claude in Amazon Bedrock runs on AWS-managed infrastructure where Anthropic personnel have no access to inference infrastructure, and data handling is governed by Amazon Bedrock (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-amazon-bedrock)

On Claude Platform on AWS Anthropic processes inference data, and for workspaces created before 2026-09-18 00:00 UTC Anthropic might process and store data outside AWS (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws)

Organizations needing FedRAMP High, IL4/IL5, HIPAA readiness or AWS as sole processor are directed to Bedrock instead of Claude Platform on AWS (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws)

Claude Platform on AWS supports CMEK via /v1/organizations/external_keys (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws ; https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/admin-api)

Foundry Hosted on Azure keeps prompts and completions within Azure; only usage metadata and content flagged by Anthropic safety systems egress to Anthropic, and Anthropic acts as an independent processor for Microsoft (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry)
Claude Code applies an Amazon Bedrock Guardrail via X-Amzn-Bedrock-GuardrailIdentifier and X-Amzn-Bedrock-GuardrailVersion custom headers (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/amazon-bedrock)

Anthropic compliance attestations (names only) are SOC 2 Type I and Type II, ISO 27001:2022, ISO/IEC 42001:2023 and a HIPAA-ready configuration (BAA available); FedRAMP High and IL4/IL5 are referenced only as reasons to use Claude via Bedrock (https://privacy.claude.com/en/articles/10015870-what-certifications-has-anthropic-obtained ; https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws)
https://trust.anthropic.com/ resolves (HTTP 200) but is a JavaScript app whose content did not render for text fetch (https://trust.anthropic.com/)
The HIPAA Implementation Guide is listed under trust.anthropic.com/resources (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/api-and-data-retention)
The Claude API is billed per token in USD per million tokens (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing)

Claude pricing pages are https://claude.com/pricing (www.anthropic.com/pricing redirects there) and https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing)
Claude Fable 5.2 was priced at $8 input / $40 output per MTok as shown 2026-11-14 (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing)
Claude Opus 5.5 was priced at $4 input / $20 output per MTok as shown 2026-11-14 (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing)
Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Sonnet 5 were priced at $2 input / $10 output per MTok as shown 2026-11-14 (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing)
Claude Haiku 5.5 was priced at $0.10/$0.50 per MTok for prompts up to 100k tokens and $0.50/$2.50 over 100k as shown 2026-11-14 (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing)
Claude Haiku 4.5 was priced at $1/$5 per MTok as shown 2026-11-14 (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing)

Other Claude prices shown 2026-11-14 (input/output per MTok): Fable 5.1 and Fable 5 $10/$50; Opus 5 and Opus 4.5 to 4.8 $5/$25; Sonnet 4.5/4.6 $3/$15 (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing)

Claude prompt caching multipliers shown 2026-11-14: 5-minute cache write 1.25x base input, 1-hour cache write 2x, cache read 0.1x on most models, 0.05x on Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5, 0.025x on Fable/Mythos 5.1 and 5.2; multipliers stack with batch and data residency (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing)
The Claude Batch API discount is 50% on input and output as shown 2026-11-14 (e.g. Opus 5.5 batch $2/$10 per MTok) (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing)
Claude fast mode is not available with the Batch API (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing)

Claude fast mode is a premium speed tier with up to 2.5x output tokens/second, priced as shown 2026-11-14 at Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 $16/$80, Opus 5.5 $8/$40, and Opus 5/4.8 $10/$50 per MTok (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing)
On Claude 4.6+ models the 1M-token context window is billed at standard pricing, except Haiku 5.5, which has a 100k-token price threshold (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing)

Claude Priority Tier capacity commitments (input/output TPM, 1/3/6/12 months, specific model, 99.5% uptime target) are legacy and no longer available for purchase; existing commitments run to contract end (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/service-tiers)
The service_tier parameter accepts "auto" or "standard_only", and Priority Tier is not supported on Claude 5.x models (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/service-tiers)

Claude API usage tier monthly spend caps are Start $500, Build $1,000 and Scale $200,000; Custom has no cap, and new organizations may start in an Evaluation tier (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/rate-limits)
At the usage tier spend cap Claude API requests return 429 rate_limit_error with error_code: enforced_spend_limit_reached and no retry-after (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/rate-limits)

Claude Console org admins set a monthly spend limit at platform.claude.com/settings/spend-limits up to the tier cap, and workspace monthly spend limits are set on the Workspaces page (not on the Default Workspace) (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/rate-limits ; https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workspaces)
Hitting a self-set Claude spend limit returns 400 invalid_request_error (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/rate-limits)

Claude workspace rate limits are set per model and limiter (RPM, ITPM and OTPM) below org limits via the Console Rate limits page or the Rate Limits API; ITPM counts only uncached input plus cache writes (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/rate-limits)
The Claude Rate Limits API was released on 2026-04-24 (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/release-notes/overview)
The Claude Free plan was $0 as shown 2026-11-14 (https://claude.com/pricing)

Claude Max was $100/month as shown 2026-11-14 (https://claude.com/pricing)
Claude Ultra was $200/month as shown 2026-11-14 (https://claude.com/pricing)

Claude Enterprise was $20/seat/month billed annually with a 20-seat minimum, plus usage at API rates, as shown 2026-11-14 (https://claude.com/pricing)
Claude Max plans include monthly API credits since 2026-10-07 (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/release-notes/overview)
Claude Ultra plans include monthly API credits since 2026-10-07 (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/release-notes/overview)
Claude Team plans include monthly API credits since 2026-10-07 (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/release-notes/overview)
Claude Enterprise per-user spend limits are managed via the Spend Limits API, which requires the read:spend_limits scope to read (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/admin-api-keys)
Changing Claude Enterprise per-user spend limits via the Spend Limits API requires the write:spend_limits scope (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/admin-api-keys)
The Claude Spend Limits API is called with an Enterprise admin key carrying read:spend_limits / write:spend_limits scopes (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/admin-api-keys)

Claude Platform on AWS and Foundry usage is rated at standard per-model rates, discounted, converted at $0.01 per CCU, metered hourly to AWS Marketplace or Azure Marketplace, and invoiced monthly in arrears with no prepaid credits (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing)
Claude Platform on AWS bills in Claude Consumption Units (CCUs) metered hourly to AWS Marketplace (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing)
Claude in Microsoft Foundry bills in Claude Consumption Units (CCUs) metered hourly to Azure Marketplace (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing)

GET /v1/models returns max_input_tokens, max_tokens, a capabilities object (including thinking.types.disabled, server_tools.web_search, server_tools.code_execution) and a line field (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/overview)
The Models API line field was added on 2026-10-01 (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/release-notes/overview)
Current Claude models use adaptive thinking steered by output_config.effort (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/overview)
Manual extended thinking (thinking.type: "enabled" with budget_tokens) is deprecated on Opus 4.6/Sonnet 4.6 and returns a 400 on Claude 4.7 and later (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/errors)
Fable 5.x, Mythos 5.x and Opus 5.5 reject thinking: {"type": "disabled"} (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/errors)
Claude Sonnet 5.5 uses thinking: {"type": "between_tools"} as its lowest thinking setting (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/errors)
Claude Haiku 5.5 accepts thinking type disabled (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/errors)

Fable 5.2, Mythos 5.2, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 return a 400 for tool_choice any or tool; use auto with strict tool use or structured outputs instead (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/errors)

Claude structured outputs are stable: JSON outputs use output_config.format with type: "json_schema" and strict tool use uses strict: true on a tool, stable on the Claude API, Bedrock, Claude Platform on AWS, both Google Cloud offerings and Microsoft Foundry (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/structured-outputs)
Claude structured outputs do not support recursive schemas or numeric/length constraints (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/structured-outputs)
Claude prompt caching default TTL is 5 minutes (write 1.25x base input) with an optional 1-hour TTL ("ttl": "1h", write 2x) (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching)

Claude prompt caching allows up to 4 explicit cache_control breakpoints, and the minimum cacheable length is 512 tokens on Opus 5.5/Sonnet 5.5/Haiku 5.5 (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching)
Automatic caching via a top-level cache_control field is not available on Bedrock bedrock-runtime (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching)

Claude prompt caches are isolated per workspace on the Claude API, Claude Platform on AWS and Microsoft Foundry, but only per organization on Bedrock and Claude Models on Google Cloud (Google managed) (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching)
The Claude Message Batches API is POST /v1/messages/batches and gives 50% off (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing)

A Claude message batch holds up to 100,000 requests or 256 MB, expires if not done within 24 hours, and results are downloadable for 29 days (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing)

Message Batches support up to 300K output tokens with beta header output-300k-2026-03-24 on supported models (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing ; https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/overview)
Claude citations return exact supporting passages from documents (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/overview)
search_result content blocks let you supply your own retrieval results so Claude cites them like web search results (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/overview)
The Claude API has no hosted vector store; retrieval is bring-your-own (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/overview)
Claude context editing is beta under context-management-2025-06-27 and clears old tool results and thinking (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/beta-headers)

Claude threshold compaction is beta under compact-2026-01-12 with edit type compact_20260112 and a default trigger of 150,000 input tokens (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/compaction-threshold)
Claude on-demand compaction entered beta on 2026-09-14 under compact-2026-09-04 (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/release-notes/overview)

Claude message threads entered beta on 2026-11-02 under message-threads-2026-08-12, letting long-running agents send only new messages per request for faster time to first token (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/release-notes/overview ; https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/overview)
The SDK tool runner (client.beta.messages.tool_runner) runs the client tool-use loop (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/overview)
The Claude tool search tool lets Claude load only needed tool definitions (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/overview)
Programmatic tool calling lets Claude call your tools from code inside the code execution container (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/overview)

The Claude web search tool is stable, with versions web_search_20250305 (basic), web_search_20260209 (dynamic filtering) and web_search_20260318 (response inclusion) (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-search-tool)
The Claude web search tool is priced at $10 per 1,000 searches plus tokens as shown 2026-11-14 (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-search-tool)
Claude web search tool parameters are max_uses, allowed_domains or blocked_domains (not both) and user_location (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-search-tool)

The Claude web fetch tool is stable, with versions web_fetch_20250910, web_fetch_20260209, web_fetch_20260309 (cache bypass) and web_fetch_20260318, and has no extra charge beyond tokens (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-fetch-tool)
The Claude web fetch tool can fetch only URLs that already appeared in the conversation and does not render JavaScript (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-fetch-tool)

The Claude code execution tool is stable with no beta header, with versions code_execution_20250825, code_execution_20260120 (REPL state, programmatic tool calling) and code_execution_20260521 (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/code-execution-tool)
Claude code execution containers have 5 GiB RAM, 5 GiB disk, 1 CPU, no internet, and expire 30 days after creation (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/code-execution-tool)

Claude code execution includes 1,550 free hours per organization per month, then $0.05 per container-hour, and is free when used with web_search_20260209/web_fetch_20260209 or later (shown 2026-11-14) (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/code-execution-tool)

The Claude memory tool is ZDR eligible (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/memory-tool)

Fable 5.2, Mythos 5.2, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 use computer_toolset_20260801 with no beta header, GA since 2026-08-19 (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/computer-use-tool ; https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/release-notes/overview)

Older Claude models use computer_20251124 (beta computer-use-2025-11-24), and for computer use you supply the VM or container (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/computer-use-tool)
Computer use is not available in Claude Managed Agents (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/computer-use-tool)
The Claude browser use tool browser_toolset_20260801 launched on 2026-08-19 as a client tool where your application drives a browser (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/release-notes/overview)
The Python and TypeScript SDKs ship browser and computer use toolset classes (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/overview)
The Claude Files API is GA since 2026-08-19 and needs no beta header (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/files ; https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/release-notes/overview)

POST /v1/files accepts files up to 500 MB, 1 TB total per organization, roughly 500 requests per minute, with optional expires_in_seconds from 3,600 to 7,776,000 (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/files)
Files uploaded to the Claude Files API are not downloadable; only skill/code-execution outputs are (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/files)

Claude Managed Agents is exposed at /v1/agents, /v1/sessions and /v1/environments, all requiring beta header managed-agents-2026-04-01 (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/overview)

Claude Agent SDK packages are Python claude-agent-sdk (PyPI 0.2.182, Python 3.10+) and TypeScript @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk (npm 0.3.325, Node.js 18.14+) (https://pypi.org/pypi/claude-agent-sdk/json ; https://registry.npmjs.org/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/latest)

Third-party products built on the Agent SDK must use API key authentication (or Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry/Claude Platform on AWS via CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK=1, CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX=1, CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY=1, CLAUDE_CODE_USE_ANTHROPIC_AWS=1), not claude.ai login, unless Anthropic has approved it (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/quickstart)

Claude Code has 33 hook events (including PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PermissionRequest, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, SubagentStop, SessionStart, SessionEnd, PreCompact) and hook types command, http, mcp_tool, prompt and agent (experimental) (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks)

Claude Code skills are SKILL.md instruction packages; a skill saved in ~/.claude/skills/ is available in every project, and project skills live in .claude/skills/ (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/overview ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless)

Claude OpenTelemetry tracing has been beta since 2026-10-14: the Claude API can export spans for model requests, tool uses and Managed Agents sessions, and the Anthropic SDKs emit spans for requests and tool-runner calls (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/overview ; https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/release-notes/overview)

The Claude MCP connector is beta: pass mcp_servers (type url, url, name, optional authorization_token) plus a matching {"type": "mcp_toolset", "mcp_server_name": ...} in tools, with beta header mcp-client-2026-09-15 (adds tool-list pinning) or mcp-client-2025-11-20; mcp-client-2025-04-04 is deprecated (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-connector)

The Claude MCP connector supports only MCP tool calls (no resources or prompts) on servers publicly reachable over Streamable HTTP or SSE (no local stdio) (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-connector)

With the Claude MCP connector the caller must run the OAuth flow and pass the access token; it is not ZDR eligible and is beta on the Claude API, Claude Platform on AWS, Claude Models on Google Cloud (Anthropic managed) and Microsoft Foundry (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-connector)

Claude MCP tunnels (research preview) are outbound-only tunnels (cloudflared plus an Anthropic proxy, Helm or Docker Compose) that expose private-network MCP servers to the Messages API MCP connector and Managed Agents (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/overview)

The Claude MCP tunnels management API is at /v1/tunnels, moved from /v1/organizations/tunnels on 2026-06-22 (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/overview ; https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/release-notes/overview)
Claude MCP tunnels are not available as claude.ai connectors (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/overview)

The Anthropic SDKs include helpers that convert between MCP and Claude API types for running your own MCP client (local servers, prompts, resources) (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/overview)

The Claude Platform Docs MCP server com.claude.platform/docs is a remote Streamable HTTP server at https://platform.claude.com/docs/mcp that searches and reads the Claude Platform docs and API reference (https://platform.claude.com/docs/mcp/server-card ; https://platform.claude.com/llms.txt)
The Claude Platform Docs MCP server card is at https://platform.claude.com/docs/mcp/server-card (https://platform.claude.com/docs/mcp/server-card)

Remote MCP servers can be added by URL as custom connectors on Free (one connector), Pro, Max, Ultra, Team and Enterprise plans (https://claude.com/docs/connectors/custom/remote-mcp ; https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11175166-get-started-with-custom-connectors-using-remote-mcp.md)
On Team/Enterprise an Owner adds custom connectors under Organization settings > Connectors and members connect individually (https://claude.com/docs/connectors/custom/remote-mcp)
Claude connects to custom connectors from Anthropic's cloud, not the user's device (https://claude.com/docs/connectors/custom/remote-mcp)

Claude apps connector authentication options are Claude's published identity (Client ID Metadata Document, recommended), Dynamic Client Registration, or your own OAuth client; static request headers (up to four, beta, limited orgs) suit API-key servers (https://claude.com/docs/connectors/custom/remote-mcp)
A connector URL ending /sse selects the older SSE transport, and connector auth settings cannot be edited after adding (https://claude.com/docs/connectors/custom/remote-mcp)

Claude Desktop installs local MCP servers packaged as .mcpb (MCP Bundles) desktop extensions under Settings > Extensions, and organizations can restrict them (https://claude.com/docs/connectors/custom/remote-mcp)

Anthropic's Connectors Directory lists verified and community MCP connectors, and Anthropic said in December 2025 it held over 75 MCP-powered connectors (https://claude.com/docs/connectors/custom/remote-mcp ; https://www.anthropic.com/news/donating-the-model-context-protocol-and-establishing-of-the-agentic-ai-foundation)

The current MCP specification version is 2026-07-28; prior versions are 2025-11-25, 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26 and 2024-11-05 (https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/latest ; https://modelcontextprotocol.io/llms.txt)

MCP 2026-07-28 is stateless: it removes the initialize handshake and Mcp-Session-Id sessions from Streamable HTTP, adds server/discover, replaces the GET stream and resource subscribe with subscriptions/listen, introduces Multi Round-Trip Requests (InputRequiredResult), removes SSE resumability, and moves tasks to the io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks extension (https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/changelog)

MCP 2026-07-28 deprecates Roots, Sampling and Logging, formally deprecates the HTTP+SSE transport (migrate to Streamable HTTP), and deprecates Dynamic Client Registration in favor of Client ID Metadata Documents, with a minimum deprecation window of twelve months (https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/changelog)

MCP authorization is based on OAuth 2.1 and is optional; HTTP transports should follow it and stdio should use environment credentials (https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization)

MCP servers MUST publish RFC 9728 Protected Resource Metadata, clients MUST use RFC 8707 resource indicators and PKCE, and clients SHOULD support Client ID Metadata Documents and validate RFC 9207 iss (https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization)
