MCP clients can authenticate to Google Cloud MCP servers with an OAuth client ID and secret (https://docs.cloud.google.com/mcp/configure-mcp-ai-application).

To connect Claude.ai, Claude Code or Claude Desktop to a Google Cloud MCP server, create a Web application OAuth client under Google Auth Platform > Clients with redirect URI https://claude.ai/api/mcp/auth_callback, then add a custom connector with the MCP URL and put the client ID and secret in Advanced settings (https://docs.cloud.google.com/mcp/configure-mcp-ai-application).

Workspace MCP servers are Developer Preview, for example Gmail https://gmailmcp.googleapis.com/mcp/v1 and Drive https://drivemcp.googleapis.com/mcp/v1; other Google servers include Maps Grounding Lite and the Developer Knowledge API (https://docs.cloud.google.com/mcp/supported-products).

MCP Toolbox for Databases (googleapis/mcp-toolbox) is the new name of genai-toolbox (Gen AI Toolbox for Databases), Google's open-source MCP server for databases (https://github.com/googleapis/mcp-toolbox).
The latest MCP Toolbox for Databases release is v1.17.0 (2026-11-13) (https://github.com/googleapis/mcp-toolbox).

MCP Toolbox sources include AlloyDB, BigQuery, Cloud SQL, Spanner, Firestore and Knowledge Catalog, plus PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, Oracle, MongoDB, Redis, Snowflake, Neo4j, ClickHouse, Trino and others (https://github.com/googleapis/mcp-toolbox).
MCP Toolbox docs are at https://mcp-toolbox.dev/ (https://github.com/googleapis/mcp-toolbox).

MCP Toolbox runs from a binary, npx or Go with stdio or HTTP transport; the Windows binary is https://storage.googleapis.com/mcp-toolbox-for-databases/v1.17.0/windows/amd64/toolbox.exe, and HTTP runs on default port 5000 at /mcp or /mcp/{toolset} (https://github.com/googleapis/mcp-toolbox).
npx -y @toolbox-sdk/server --prebuilt=bigquery --stdio runs the prebuilt BigQuery MCP Toolbox over stdio, and custom tools go in --config tools.yaml (https://github.com/googleapis/mcp-toolbox).

MCP Toolbox client SDKs: Python toolbox-core, toolbox-langchain and toolbox-llamaindex; JS @toolbox-sdk/core and @toolbox-sdk/adk; Go github.com/googleapis/mcp-toolbox-sdk-go; Java com.google.cloud.mcp:mcp-toolbox-sdk-java (https://github.com/googleapis/mcp-toolbox).
toolbox-core was at 1.4.0 on 2026-09-01 (https://pypi.org/project/toolbox-core/).

ADK agents call external MCP servers through McpToolset with connection classes StdioConnectionParams, StreamableHTTPConnectionParams and SseConnectionParams; MCP is supported in Python, TypeScript (MCPToolset), Go, Java and Kotlin (https://adk.dev/tools-custom/mcp-tools/).
Production ADK agents must define McpToolset synchronously in agent.py (https://adk.dev/tools-custom/mcp-tools/).
Cloud Run hosts custom MCP servers over Streamable HTTP but not stdio (https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/host-mcp-servers).

Clients of a Cloud Run-hosted MCP server authenticate with Cloud Run Invoker via gcloud run services proxy NAME --region REGION --port=3000, an OIDC ID token, or IAP (https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/host-mcp-servers).
Deploying to Cloud Run with --functional-type=mcp-server registers the MCP server in Agent Registry automatically (https://docs.cloud.google.com/agent-registry/register-mcp-servers).

Agent Runtime lists A2A deployment as supported, with A2A multi-agent systems marked preview; A2A is also supported on Cloud Run and Agent Registry (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/build/runtime).
A2A agents serve /.well-known/agent-card.json, which Agent Registry reads to extract skills (https://docs.cloud.google.com/agent-registry/register-mcp-servers).
ADK consumes remote A2A agents through RemoteA2aAgent (https://codelabs.developers.google.com/adk-a2a-agent-runtime).
adkgo deploy cloudrun enables --a2a by default (https://adk.dev/deploy/cloud-run/).

A2A methods on Agent Runtime have their own quotas: POST methods (sendMessage, cancelTask) at 60 per minute and GET methods (getTask, getCard) at 600 per minute (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/resources/agent-quotas).

Apigee hosts MCP servers for existing APIs through the MCP Discovery Proxy: each OpenAPI 3.0.0-3.0.3 operation becomes an MCP tool behind ORG_NAME.mcp.apigee.internal, using JSON-RPC tools/list and tools/call (https://docs.cloud.google.com/apigee/docs/api-platform/apigee-mcp/apigee-mcp-overview).
The Apigee MCP Discovery Proxy authenticates with OAuth 2.1 or OIDC (https://docs.cloud.google.com/apigee/docs/api-platform/apigee-mcp/apigee-mcp-overview).

Apigee MCP is available on Subscription, Pay-as-you-go, Evaluation and Data Residency organizations, and on Apigee hybrid 1.17.0 or later (https://docs.cloud.google.com/apigee/docs/api-platform/apigee-mcp/apigee-mcp-overview).

The Apigee API hub MCP server went GA on 2026-07-24, with endpoints https://apihub.googleapis.com/mcp (global) and https://apihub.REGION.rep.googleapis.com/mcp (https://docs.cloud.google.com/apigee/docs/apihub/release-notes).
The Apigee API hub MCP server integrates with Model Armor (https://docs.cloud.google.com/apigee/docs/apihub/release-notes).

gcloud apihub locations configure-and-deploy-server (2026-08-12), like the ConfigureAndDeployServer RPC (2026-07-24), bundles API operations into MCP servers deployed on Apigee (https://docs.cloud.google.com/apigee/docs/apihub/release-notes).
API hub syncs MCP metadata to Agent Registry by default (https://docs.cloud.google.com/apigee/docs/apihub/register-mcp-apis).

ADK reaches Application Integration and Integration Connectors through the Python class google.adk.tools.application_integration_tool.application_integration_toolset.ApplicationIntegrationToolset (with a Java equivalent), using integration= with triggers for workflows (https://adk.dev/integrations/application-integration/).
ApplicationIntegrationToolset uses connection= with entity_operations and actions for Integration Connectors (https://adk.dev/integrations/application-integration/).
ApplicationIntegrationToolset needs roles/integrations.integrationEditor, roles/connectors.invoker and roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor (https://adk.dev/integrations/application-integration/).
ApplicationIntegrationToolset needs roles/connectors.invoker to call Integration Connectors (https://adk.dev/integrations/application-integration/).
ApplicationIntegrationToolset needs roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor (https://adk.dev/integrations/application-integration/).

Integration Connectors has 147 connectors, 35 for Google services and 112 for other applications, with GA connectors including Salesforce, ServiceNow, Snowflake, SharePoint, Workday, Microsoft Dynamics 365 and the SAP family (ERP, HANA, SuccessFactors, Ariba) (https://docs.cloud.google.com/integration-connectors/docs/connector-reference-overview).
Databricks was not listed among Integration Connectors connectors (https://docs.cloud.google.com/integration-connectors/docs/connector-reference-overview).
Integration Connectors added an MCP connector (client side) in preview on 2025-12-16 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/integration-connectors/docs/release-notes).

The Integration Connectors MCP connector has versions v1 and v2 for MCP API versions and allocates 2 nodes per connection by default (https://docs.cloud.google.com/integration-connectors/docs/connectors/mcp/overview-mcp).
The MCP connector is used from Application Integration via the Connectors task (https://docs.cloud.google.com/integration-connectors/docs/connectors/mcp/overview-mcp).

The Conversational Analytics API has native SDKs in seven languages: Python, Java, Go, Node.js, PHP, Ruby and .NET (https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/data-analytics/build-data-agents-with-conversational-analytics-api).
The Conversational Analytics API global endpoint is geminidataanalytics.googleapis.com (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/data-agents/conversational-analytics-api/data-residency).
gcloud run deploy --source . builds and deploys from source, and --image deploys an existing image (https://adk.dev/deploy/cloud-run/).
Cloud Run services are private by default unless --allow-unauthenticated is set (https://adk.dev/deploy/cloud-run/).
Authenticated Cloud Run calls use Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-identity-token) (https://adk.dev/deploy/cloud-run/).

Install the gcloud CLI on Windows with winget install --id Google.CloudSDK (version 593.0.0 on winget as of 2026-11-14) or the installer https://dl.google.com/dl/cloudsdk/channels/rapid/GoogleCloudSDKInstaller.exe (https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/docs/install-sdk).
The gcloud CLI on Windows needs Windows 8.1+ or Server 2012+, supports Python 3.10-3.15 and bundles Python by default (https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/docs/install-sdk).
The current gcloud CLI is 593.0.0, released 2026-11-10; release 591.0.0 updated bundled Python to 3.14.9 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/docs/release-notes).
In gcloud 593.0.0, bundled Python became a required component on Windows x86/x86_64 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/docs/release-notes).
gcloud init authorizes and creates a default configuration (--console-only skips the browser), and gcloud auth login signs in the CLI itself (https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/docs/install-sdk).
gcloud auth application-default login creates the separate ADC file that client libraries, ADK and MCP clients use (https://docs.cloud.google.com/docs/authentication/application-default-credentials).

ADC searches in a fixed order: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS, then the gcloud ADC file, then the attached service account via the metadata server (https://docs.cloud.google.com/docs/authentication/application-default-credentials).

The ADC file is %APPDATA%\gcloud\application_default_credentials.json on Windows and $HOME/.config/gcloud/application_default_credentials.json on Linux and macOS (https://docs.cloud.google.com/docs/authentication/application-default-credentials).
ADC user tokens expire about every hour (https://docs.cloud.google.com/mcp/configure-mcp-ai-application).

Service account impersonation is set per command with --impersonate-service-account=SA_EMAIL, for the whole CLI with gcloud config set auth/impersonate_service_account SA_EMAIL, or for ADC with gcloud auth application-default login --impersonate-service-account SA_EMAIL (https://docs.cloud.google.com/docs/authentication/use-service-account-impersonation).
Service account impersonation needs roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator on the target service account (https://docs.cloud.google.com/docs/authentication/use-service-account-impersonation).
Service account impersonation needs iamcredentials.googleapis.com enabled (https://docs.cloud.google.com/docs/authentication/use-service-account-impersonation).

gcloud command groups for agent work are gcloud ai (models, endpoints, semantic-governance-policies GA in 581.0.0), gcloud agent-registry (skills, revisions, publishers and findings GA in 591.0.0), gcloud agent-identity auth-providers (authorizations GA in 593.0.0), gcloud run deploy and gcloud services enable (https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/docs/release-notes).

The old gcloud MCP command groups were removed in favor of Agent Registry: gcloud api-registry mcp enable|disable (579.0.0), gcloud beta services mcp enable|disable|list (581.0.0), and gcloud api-registry mcp servers list|tools list and gcloud beta services mcp policies (582.0.0) (https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/docs/release-notes).

The gcloud MCP command groups (api-registry mcp, beta services mcp) were removed between releases 579.0.0 and 582.0.0 in favor of Agent Registry (https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/docs/release-notes).

bq is the Python-based BigQuery CLI that ships with the gcloud CLI, authenticates through gcloud (--use_gcloud_config defaults to true) and honors auth/impersonate_service_account (https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/bq-cli-reference).

bq defaults go in $HOME/.bigqueryrc or the path in BIGQUERYRC; put --use_legacy_sql=false under [query] to make GoogleSQL the default; global flags include --project_id, --location and --format=prettyjson (https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/bq-cli-reference).

adk deploy cloud_run --project=P --region=R --service_name=S [--with_ui] AGENT_PATH deploys to Cloud Run (gcloud flags passed after --), and adk deploy agent_engine --project=P --region=R --display_name=... AGENT_DIR deploys to Agent Runtime; the Go equivalents are adkgo deploy cloudrun and adkgo deploy agentengine (https://adk.dev/deploy/cloud-run/ ; https://adk.dev/deploy/agent-runtime/deploy/).
adk deploy agent_engine and adkgo deploy agentengine deploy ADK agents to Agent Runtime (https://adk.dev/deploy/agent-runtime/deploy/).
adk deploy cloud_run and adkgo deploy cloudrun deploy ADK agents to Cloud Run (https://adk.dev/deploy/cloud-run/).
On Cloud Run, ADK sessions and artifacts are in memory and are lost when instances recycle unless you pass --session_service_uri and --artifact_service_uri (https://adk.dev/deploy/cloud-run/).
ADK on Cloud Run keeps sessions and artifacts in memory without --session_service_uri and --artifact_service_uri, so they are lost when instances recycle (https://adk.dev/deploy/cloud-run/).
Agents CLI (google-agents-cli, repo google/agents-cli) is at 1.14.0 on PyPI (2026-11-12) (https://pypi.org/project/google-agents-cli/).
Install Agents CLI with uvx google-agents-cli setup or uv tool install google-agents-cli (https://adk.dev/deploy/agent-runtime/agents-cli/).

Agents CLI handles scaffold, evaluate, deploy, publish and observe, with commands including agents-cli scaffold enhance --deployment-target agent_runtime, agents-cli deploy (also targets Cloud Run and GKE), agents-cli infra single-project and agents-cli eval run (https://google.github.io/agents-cli/guide/getting-started/index.md).
agents-cli deploy deploys agents to Agent Runtime and also targets Cloud Run and GKE (https://adk.dev/deploy/agent-runtime/agents-cli/).
The Terraform Google provider is hashicorp/google 8.11.0 (2026-11-10), with a companion hashicorp/google-beta (https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/google/latest/docs).

Agent Runtime is managed in Terraform with google_vertex_ai_reasoning_engine (provider >= 5.28.0, Terraform >= 1.5.0) plus google_vertex_ai_reasoning_engine_iam_* resources (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/scale/runtime/use-terraform).
Agent Gateway configuration in Terraform needs the google-beta provider (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/scale/runtime/use-terraform).

The google_vertex_ai_reasoning_engine resource has three spec options: container_spec { image_uri } (port 8080), source_code_spec { inline_source { source_archive } } with an empty image_spec {}, and package_spec (pickle in GCS) (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/scale/runtime/use-terraform).

spec.identity_type = "AGENT_IDENTITY" is required when agent_gateway_config is set on google_vertex_ai_reasoning_engine (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/scale/runtime/use-terraform).
Pulumi @pulumi/gcp manages Agent Runtime with vertex AiReasoningEngine* resources (https://www.pulumi.com/registry/packages/gcp/api-docs/vertex/aireasoningengineiampolicy/).

The Ansible google.cloud collection manages Agent Runtime with the gcp_vertexai_reasoning_engine module; Agents CLI also generates Terraform templates (https://docs.ansible.com/projects/ansible/13/collections/google/cloud/gcp_vertexai_reasoning_engine_module.html).

Google Cloud docs moved to the docs.cloud.google.com host: https://cloud.google.com/docs returns 301 to https://docs.cloud.google.com/docs, https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs returns 301 to https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs (now the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform landing page) (https://docs.cloud.google.com/docs).
Agent Platform docs pages sit under https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/ (https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs).

Google Cloud docs have no llms.txt: https://docs.cloud.google.com/llms.txt and /llms-full.txt returned 404 on 2026-11-14, and https://cloud.google.com/llms.txt returns an HTML page (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/standard-paygo.md.txt).

Appending .md.txt to a Google Cloud docs page path returns Markdown (text/markdown), for example https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/standard-paygo.md.txt (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/standard-paygo.md.txt).

The Developer Knowledge MCP server (https://developerknowledge.googleapis.com/mcp) is Google's docs MCP server covering public English Google developer docs including Google Cloud, Firebase, Android and Maps, with tools search_documents, get_documents and answer_query (https://developers.google.com/knowledge/mcp).
The Developer Knowledge MCP server authenticates with an API key in X-Goog-Api-Key or with OAuth/ADC (https://developers.google.com/knowledge/mcp).
Enable the Developer Knowledge MCP server with gcloud services enable developerknowledge.googleapis.com (https://developers.google.com/knowledge/mcp).
ADK docs are at https://adk.dev/, with https://adk.dev/llms.txt and https://adk.dev/llms-full.txt (source repo github.com/google/adk-docs) (https://adk.dev/llms.txt).
MCP Toolbox docs are at https://mcp-toolbox.dev/, with https://mcp-toolbox.dev/llms.txt (https://mcp-toolbox.dev/llms.txt).
Agent Platform release notes are at https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes).
gcloud release notes are at https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/docs/release-notes (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes).
Apigee API hub release notes are at https://docs.cloud.google.com/apigee/docs/apihub/release-notes (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes).
Integration Connectors release notes are at https://docs.cloud.google.com/integration-connectors/docs/release-notes (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes).
Application Integration release notes are at https://docs.cloud.google.com/application-integration/docs/release-notes (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes).

Conversational Analytics release notes are at https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/data-agents/conversational-analytics-api/release-notes (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes).

MCP reference pages are the overview at https://docs.cloud.google.com/mcp/overview and the endpoint list at https://docs.cloud.google.com/mcp/supported-products (https://docs.cloud.google.com/mcp/supported-products).
The Google Cloud status page is https://status.cloud.google.com/, which resolved on 2026-11-14 (https://status.cloud.google.com/).

Official samples and codelabs include github.com/google/adk-python (v2.14.1, 2026-11-12), github.com/google/agents-cli, github.com/googleapis/mcp-toolbox and the codelab https://codelabs.developers.google.com/adk-a2a-agent-runtime (A2A on Agent Runtime) (https://github.com/google/adk-python ; https://codelabs.developers.google.com/adk-a2a-agent-runtime).
The Agents CLI codelab is https://codelabs.developers.google.com/agents-cli-agent-platform/agents-cli-agent-platform (https://github.com/google/adk-python).

Standard PayGo replaced dynamic shared quota as the documented model for Gemini on Agent Platform, and the old /vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/dsq URL now serves the Standard PayGo page (https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/dsq).

Under Standard PayGo, Gemini usage runs on shared capacity with an organization-level usage tier set by eligible spend over a rolling 30 days (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/deploy/standard-paygo).
A Standard PayGo tier's TPM threshold is the level below which traffic is prioritized, not a hard cap (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/deploy/standard-paygo).

Standard PayGo TPM thresholds as shown 2026-11-14: Pro, Carbon and Argon get Tier 1 ($10-$250) 500K, Tier 2 ($250-$2,000) 1M, Tier 3 ($2,000-$50,000) 2M and Tier 4 (above $50,000) 10M; Flash, Flash-Lite and Hydrogen get 2M, 4M, 10M and 50M; there is no separate RPM limit and preview models are excluded (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/deploy/standard-paygo).
Standard PayGo Tier 4 was added on 2026-09-10 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes).

A 429 on Standard PayGo means temporary contention for shared capacity, not an exhausted fixed quota; the fixes are exponential backoff, smoothing per-second spikes, and using the global endpoint (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/deploy/standard-paygo).

For Gemini, the global endpoint draws on a worldwide pool and gets the full tier threshold but gives no data residency guarantee; multi-region us and eu use separate pools; single-region endpoints such as us-central1 have the least headroom; Google recommends global unless residency requires otherwise (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/deploy/standard-paygo).
Org policy can block global endpoint traffic on Agent Platform (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/resources/data-residency).

Gemini models older than Gemini 3 are not served on the jurisdictional multi-region endpoints and stay on regional endpoints, and calling a model at an endpoint type it does not support returns a 404 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/resources/data-residency ; https://www.braintrust.dev/docs/kb/vertex-ai-gemini-model-region-and-registry-issues.md (secondary)).

Priority PayGo (preview) costs more per token than Standard PayGo but gives more consistent throughput, with no commitment, and responses report ON_DEMAND_PRIORITY as the traffic type (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/priority-paygo).
Priority PayGo ramp limits were removed on 2026-09-10 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes).
Priority PayGo endpoint support (global, or global plus us/eu) differs between page versions (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/priority-paygo).
Flex PayGo (preview) is 50% off Standard PayGo, for latency-tolerant work (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/deploy/flex-paygo).

Flex PayGo works only on the global endpoint, allows a 20 MB payload, and accepts request timeouts up to 30 minutes (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/deploy/flex-paygo).

Provisioned Throughput is bought in GSUs (generative AI scale units) for terms of 1 week, 1 month, 3 months or 1 year (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/provisioned-throughput/use-provisioned-throughput).

Provisioned Throughput quota is GSUs times the model's per-GSU throughput, for example 2,690 tokens/s per GSU for gemini-2.5-flash and 685 tokens/s for Gemini 4 Hydrogen, enforced over a 1 to 120 second window depending on order size (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/provisioned-throughput/use-provisioned-throughput).

By default a request over the Provisioned Throughput quota spills over in full to pay-as-you-go billing; send header X-Vertex-AI-LLM-Request-Type: dedicated to get a 429 instead of overage charges, or shared to bypass Provisioned Throughput (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/provisioned-throughput/use-provisioned-throughput).

Claude models launched after 2026-05-26 share one quota per lineage per location (anthropic-claude-opus, -sonnet, -haiku, -fable and -fable-fast); global, us and eu are separate buckets, fast-mode requests use a *-fast bucket, and older Claude models use per-model QPM/TPM by endpoint type (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/partner-models/claude/quotas).

Default Claude Opus 5.5 quota as shown 2026-11-14 is 2,000 QPM, 20M input TPM and 2M output TPM on global, and half that on multi-region (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/partner-models/claude/quotas).

Default Claude Sonnet 5.5/5 quota as shown 2026-11-14 is 2,500 QPM, 25M input TPM and 2.5M output TPM on global (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/partner-models/claude/quotas).

Default Claude Sonnet 5.5/5 quota as shown 2026-11-14 is 2,500 QPM, 25M input TPM and 2.5M output TPM on global (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/partner-models/claude/quotas).

Default Claude Haiku 5.5 quota as shown 2026-11-14 is 3,000 QPM, 30M input TPM and 3M output TPM on global (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/partner-models/claude/quotas).
The Quota page's Claude token usage can be inaccurate, so use the token_count metrics (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/partner-models/claude/quotas).

New projects can show Claude quota as '0 to 0' until model access eligibility is reviewed (https://discuss.google.dev/t/anthropic-claude-quota-stuck-at-0-to-0-on-new-paid-account-requesting-manual-model-access-eligibility-review-eu-multi-region/382201 (secondary)).

Agent Runtime default quotas per project per region: Query/StreamQuery 90 per minute, BidiStreamQuery 10 concurrent live connections, 100 resources, resource create/update/delete 10 per minute, session writes 100 per minute, session event appends 300 per minute, and 950 revisions per agent (a fixed system limit) (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/resources/agent-quotas).
Agent Runtime express mode allows only 10 query requests per minute and 10 resources (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/resources/agent-quotas).

RAG Engine quotas per project per region: data-management APIs 60 RPM, RetrievalContexts 600 RPM, ImportRagFiles 3 concurrent and 10,000 files per request (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/machine-learning/quotas).
The Gen AI evaluation service quota is 1,000 RPM and 20 concurrent runs per project per region (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/machine-learning/quotas).
Agent Platform online inference quota is 30,000 RPM and CRUD calls 600 RPM per project per region (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/machine-learning/quotas).

BigQuery MCP SQL tools cancel queries after 3 minutes by default, return at most 3,000 rows, and don't support Google Drive external tables; BigQuery API quotas still apply (https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/use-bigquery-mcp).
execute_sql_readonly on the BigQuery MCP server rejects DML, DDL, Python UDFs and GQL (https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/use-bigquery-mcp).

Cloud Run limits: requests up to 60 minutes; HTTP/1 requests and responses capped at 32 MiB (except HTTP/2 and streamed responses); up to 1,000 concurrent requests, 32 GiB memory and 8 vCPU per instance; default regional cap of 100 instances per project; L4 GPU quota 0 by default (3 auto-granted to new projects) (https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/quotas).
Apigee SaaS organizations are capped at 1,000 MCP tools (https://docs.cloud.google.com/apigee/docs/api-platform/apigee-mcp/apigee-mcp-overview).
Apigee MCP provisioning may fail in europe-central2, europe-southwest1, europe-west9 and me-central2 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/apigee/docs/api-platform/apigee-mcp/apigee-mcp-overview).

GET requests on Apigee MCP error responses return 405 because SSE is not supported; Apigee hybrid does not support the stateless MCP protocol 2026-07-28, and toggling MCP there triggers a staged Message Processor restart (https://docs.cloud.google.com/apigee/docs/api-platform/apigee-mcp/apigee-mcp-overview).

Granting roles/integrations.integrationInvoker to ADK agents on Agent Runtime that use ApplicationIntegrationToolset can cause 403 errors; use roles/integrations.integrationEditor (https://adk.dev/integrations/application-integration/).

Hand-pasted ADC bearer tokens in MCP client configs expire after about an hour; for long-lived clients use an OAuth client or authProviderType: google_credentials (https://docs.cloud.google.com/mcp/configure-mcp-ai-application).
Model Armor prompt-injection filters can produce false-positive 403s on the Developer Knowledge MCP server, and HIGH_AND_ABOVE confidence is recommended (https://developers.google.com/knowledge/mcp).

A 2026-03-31 security fix requires google-cloud-aiplatform >= 1.165.1 or an explicit staging bucket (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes).

The Gemini API is a Google AI offering whose docs now live under https://aistudio.google.com/docs/* (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/billing)

As of 2026-11-14, Gemini API docs URLs https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/* return 301 redirects to https://aistudio.google.com/docs/* (for example /docs/billing, /docs/rate-limits, /docs/api-key, /docs/terms) (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/billing ; https://aistudio.google.com/docs/api-key)

The Gemini API docs publish https://aistudio.google.com/llms.txt, which lists markdown pages such as https://aistudio.google.com/docs/api-key.md and links the full corpus at https://aistudio.google.com/llms-full.txt (https://aistudio.google.com/llms.txt)
Each Gemini API key belongs to a Google Cloud project, which holds billing, collaborators and permissions (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/api-key)

Gemini API tiers, rate limits and spend caps are set per Cloud Billing account, not per project; projects linked to that billing account inherit its tier and unlinking billing returns a project to the free tier (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/billing)

To enable paid Gemini API use, select the free-tier project in AI Studio, click "Set up billing" in the Billing Tier column, choose or create a Cloud Billing account, and prepay a minimum of $5 (shown 2026-11-14) (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/billing)
The Google Agentspace experience and default app were renamed Gemini Enterprise on 2025-10-09 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/release-notes)

Gemini Enterprise docs at https://cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise/docs/* redirect (301) to https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/*, and pages also have .md.txt variants such as /docs/editions.md.txt (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs)
Gemini Enterprise Business edition covers 1-500 users with 25 GiB pooled index storage per user (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/editions)
Gemini Enterprise Standard edition covers 1 or more users with 30 GiB pooled index storage per user (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/editions)
Gemini Enterprise Plus edition covers 1 or more users with 75 GiB pooled index storage per user (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/editions)
Gemini Enterprise Pay-as-you-go edition starts at a 1-seat minimum (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/editions)
Gemini Enterprise Frontline edition requires 150 or more Standard or Plus users and has 2 GiB pooled index storage per user (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/editions)

Gemini Enterprise Pay-as-you-go edition has been GA since 2026-08-01 and was opened to all invoiced Cloud Billing accounts in September 2026 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/release-notes)

Gemini Enterprise Business edition is a web SaaS app at business.gemini.google.com; admins do not need Google Cloud console access and there are no project numbers or project-level IAM roles to manage (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/editions)

Gemini Enterprise Standard, Plus and Pay-as-you-go subscriptions are purchased per Cloud Billing account in the Cloud console on Gemini Enterprise > Plans & billing (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/licenses)

Console-purchased Gemini Enterprise seat subscriptions have a seat cap, and larger orders go through Google Cloud sales (offline order or allowlist exemption) (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/licenses)

Gemini Enterprise admin setup sequence: create or select a Cloud project, confirm billing, buy edition licenses, assign licenses (manual by email or automatic at first sign-in), grant Gemini Enterprise Admin and User roles, connect the identity provider, then create Google and third-party data stores (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/before-you-begin.md.txt)

Gemini Enterprise licenses are distributed to a specific project and location (global, us, eu, in-country), so a user needing two multi-regions needs two licenses (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/licenses)
Gemini Enterprise license distribution and reclaim in the console has been GA since 2026-06-25 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/release-notes)

Unlicensed Gemini Enterprise users have no access: removing a license ends access immediately, and on early subscription termination licenses enter a one-week deactivating grace period (GA 2026-03-17) (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/licenses)
NotebookLM Enterprise was renamed Gemini Notebook Enterprise on 2026-07-16 with unchanged API endpoints (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/release-notes)

Gemini Notebook Enterprise is sold standalone or as part of Gemini Enterprise, and notebooks are shared across both apps in the same project and location (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/notebooklm-enterprise/docs/overview)

Gemini Notebook hostnames drop "lm" on 2026-11-16 (for example notebooklm.cloud.google.com becomes notebook.cloud.google.com), and the enterprise URL pattern is notebook.cloud.google.com/REGION/?project=PROJECT_NUMBER (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/release-notes ; https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/notebooklm-enterprise/docs/overview)
The Gemini Notebook hostname change on 2026-11-16 may require network allowlists to be updated (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/release-notes)
The Workspace pricing page (2026-11-14) lists the Gemini app and Gemini in Gmail on Business Starter, Standard, Plus and Enterprise plans (https://workspace.google.com/pricing)
Gemini in Workspace comes with Workspace plans; Gemini in Docs is listed on Business Standard and up (pricing page 2026-11-14) (https://workspace.google.com/pricing)
The Workspace pricing page (2026-11-14) lists "Gemini Notebook" basic access on Business Starter and expanded access on Standard and up (https://workspace.google.com/pricing)
"AI Expanded Access" is listed as a separate Google Workspace add-on (pricing page 2026-11-14) (https://workspace.google.com/pricing)

Workspace admin help pages at support.google.com/a/answer/* redirect (301) to knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/* (https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/gemini/turn-the-gemini-app-on-or-off)

New Gemini Code Assist Standard and Enterprise subscriptions cannot be purchased from 2026-10-09; existing subscriptions auto-renew through 2026 and auto-renewal ends in 2027 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/docs/codeassist/release-notes ; https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/docs/codeassist/overview)

With Gemini Code Assist Standard and Enterprise no longer sold, Google points customers to Antigravity via eligible Gemini Enterprise subscriptions (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/docs/codeassist/overview)

From 2026-06-18 Gemini Code Assist IDE extensions stopped serving the individuals (free), Google AI Pro and Google AI Ultra tiers, and users are directed to Antigravity (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/docs/codeassist/release-notes)
Jules users sign in with a Google account at jules.google.com, accept a one-time privacy notice, and connect a GitHub account granting all or selected repositories (https://jules.google/docs)
Jules connects to a GitHub account with access to all or selected repositories (https://jules.google/docs)
Jules is described as experimental (as of 2026-11-14) (https://jules.google/docs)
Jules in Pro and Ultra (Google AI Pro / Ultra) are available only to individual @gmail.com accounts (https://jules.google/docs/usage-limits)
Jules paid plans are for consumer @gmail.com accounts only; business users are pointed to an interest form (https://jules.google/docs/usage-limits)

Day-one engagement asks: the Cloud project and billing account used for Gemini API or Gemini Enterprise; a Gemini Enterprise license plus roles/discoveryengine.agentspaceUser (builder) or roles/discoveryengine.agentspaceAdmin (admin); the identity provider and location (global/us/eu) of the Gemini Enterprise app; and for Workspace API work a service account or OAuth client plus a super admin to authorize domain-wide delegation (unverified) (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/access-control ; https://developers.google.com/workspace/guides/create-credentials)
Gemini API standard keys tie requests to a Cloud project for billing and quota but do not identify the caller (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/api-key)
Gemini API authorization (auth) keys are bound to a Google Cloud service account and run requests under that identity (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/api-key)
Gemini API auth keys are restricted to the Generative Language API by default and support fast enforcement against leaked keys (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/api-key)
All newly created AI Studio keys are auth keys from 2026-05-28 (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/api-key)
Gemini API keys created in the Cloud console must each be bound to a service account (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/api-key)
Unrestricted Gemini API standard keys must be restricted to the Gemini API, which needs the apikeys.keys.update permission (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/api-key)
The Gemini API rejects unrestricted standard keys, and from 2026-05-07 long-dormant unrestricted keys are blocked and show a "Blocked" tag in AI Studio (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/api-key)
Creating a Gemini API key requires Cloud IAM permissions such as apikeys.keys.create and iam.serviceAccounts.create (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/api-key)
Creating a Gemini API key requires iam.serviceAccounts.create among its Cloud IAM permissions (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/api-key)
Gemini client libraries read the key from GEMINI_API_KEY or GOOGLE_API_KEY, and if both are set GOOGLE_API_KEY wins (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/api-key)
The Gemini Developer API uses a Gemini API key, unlike the Cloud Gemini platform (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/migrate-to-cloud)
The Cloud Gemini platform (Vertex AI, docs slug gemini-enterprise-agent-platform) uses Cloud service accounts and IAM rather than Gemini API keys (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/migrate-to-cloud)

The google-genai SDK switches to the Cloud platform with genai.Client(vertexai=True, project=..., location=...) or genai.Client(enterprise=True, ...) for the Interactions API (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/migrate-to-cloud)

Gemini Enterprise supports Google Identity, which Google recommends and which is GA for third-party data stores since 2026-08-20 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/configure-identity-provider ; https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/release-notes)

Gemini Enterprise supports Workforce Identity Federation (Entra ID, Okta, AD FS, generic OIDC/SAML 2.0) for third-party-only setups (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/configure-identity-provider)

Gemini Enterprise Microsoft 365 ingestion (SharePoint, OneDrive, Outlook) requires Entra ID via Workforce Identity Federation (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/configure-identity-provider)

For Gemini Enterprise, create the workforce identity pool in global even for us/eu apps and map google.subject to the lowercase email, not the Entra object ID (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/configure-identity-provider)
Entra group claims for Gemini Enterprise must be filtered, with limits of 150 groups for SAML and 200 for OIDC (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/configure-identity-provider)

The Gemini Enterprise identity provider is set per location at Gemini Enterprise > Settings > Authentication > Add identity provider for global, us or eu, with one IdP type per location (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/configure-identity-provider)

Changing the Gemini Enterprise IdP type or pool requires recreating data stores and resets user IDs, losing chat history (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/configure-identity-provider)

Gemini Enterprise uses SCIM with Entra ID or Okta for large group sets and user/group autocomplete; Okta SCIM autocomplete for sharing notebooks and agents is GA since 2026-08-20 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/configure-identity-provider ; https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/release-notes)

Programmatic Gemini Enterprise API access uses Application Default Credentials (gcloud auth application-default login) or bearer tokens from gcloud auth print-access-token, or attached service accounts on Google Cloud (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/authentication)
Gemini Enterprise API access supports service account impersonation, which needs the Service Account Token Creator role (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/authentication)
Service account impersonation for Gemini Enterprise API calls requires the Service Account Token Creator role (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/authentication)
Gemini Enterprise API access supports workload identity federation from on-premises or other clouds (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/authentication)

gcloud auth application-default login sets up ADC and gcloud auth print-access-token prints a bearer token for Gemini Enterprise API calls (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/authentication)
Gemini Enterprise admins can view an agent's identity, typically a SPIFFE ID (Preview 2026-04-21) (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/release-notes)

Registering an ADK agent in Gemini Enterprise that accesses Google resources as the user requires a Web application OAuth client with redirect URIs https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/oauth-redirect and https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/static/oauth/oauth.html (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/register-and-manage-an-adk-agent)

An ADK agent acting on behalf of users in Gemini Enterprise has its OAuth client stored as an authorizations resource (serverSideOauth2) with access_type=offline and prompt=consent (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/register-and-manage-an-adk-agent)

Workspace APIs accept OAuth client IDs (Web, Android, iOS, Chrome Extension, Desktop, TV/limited input) with user consent, API keys for public data only, and service accounts (https://developers.google.com/workspace/guides/create-credentials)
Workspace APIs accept service account credentials (https://developers.google.com/workspace/guides/create-credentials)

Each Workspace OAuth client type has an optional "Use this client for an AI-powered agent" checkbox for apps acting on behalf of users; it cannot be changed after creation, and Google advises separate clients for agent and standard features (https://developers.google.com/workspace/guides/create-credentials)

Cloud IAM roles do not grant Workspace data: a service account reaches Workspace data only by being shared on files, being assigned a Workspace admin role, or via domain-wide delegation (https://developers.google.com/workspace/guides/create-credentials)

Workspace domain-wide delegation is authorised by a super admin at Admin console > Security > Access and data control > API controls > Manage Domain Wide Delegation > Add new, entering the service account or OAuth client ID and comma-delimited scopes (https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/apps/control-api-access-with-domain-wide-delegation)

With multi-party approval another super admin must approve domain-wide delegation, and changes take up to 24 hours (https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/apps/control-api-access-with-domain-wide-delegation ; https://developers.google.com/workspace/guides/create-credentials)

Gemini CLI auth modes are Sign in with Google (recommended locally), Gemini API key (GEMINI_API_KEY), or Vertex AI via ADC (gcloud auth application-default login), a service account key (GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS) or a Cloud API key (GOOGLE_API_KEY) with GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT and GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION (https://geminicli.com/docs/get-started/authentication/)
Gemini CLI can authenticate with a Gemini API key set in GEMINI_API_KEY (https://geminicli.com/docs/get-started/authentication/)
Gemini CLI can use Vertex AI via ADC (gcloud auth application-default login) (https://geminicli.com/docs/get-started/authentication/)
Gemini CLI auth settings can live in .gemini/.env (https://geminicli.com/docs/get-started/authentication/)

Company, school and Workspace accounts (including Google AI Ultra for Business) using Gemini CLI generally must set GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT, enable the Gemini for Cloud API and have IAM permissions; headless mode reuses cached credentials or env-var auth (https://geminicli.com/docs/get-started/authentication/)

Gemini Notebook Enterprise supports Cloud Identity or third-party IdPs (Entra ID, Okta, Ping, PingFederate, other OIDC/SAML 2.0) (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/notebooklm-enterprise/docs/overview)
Gemini Notebook Enterprise sharing is limited to users in the same Cloud project and public sharing is disallowed (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/notebooklm-enterprise/docs/overview)

roles/discoveryengine.agentspaceAdmin (Gemini Enterprise Admin) grants Discovery Engine Editor plus admin-only permissions such as setting agent IAM policies (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/access-control)
roles/discoveryengine.agentspaceUser (Gemini Enterprise User) allows creating, updating and deleting agents and using apps (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/access-control)

roles/discoveryengine.agentspaceRestrictedUser gives no Gemini Enterprise app access unless the user is also granted agentspaceUser per app (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/access-control)

Gemini Enterprise predefined IAM roles are roles/discoveryengine.agentspaceAdmin, roles/discoveryengine.agentspaceUser, roles/discoveryengine.agentspaceRestrictedUser, roles/discoveryengine.agentspaceViewer, roles/discoveryengine.editor and roles/discoveryengine.viewer (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/access-control)
The Gemini Enterprise Admin and User IAM role names became available 2026-04-15 and map to the existing Discovery Engine role IDs (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/release-notes)

To create agents in Agent Gallery / Workflow Builder a user needs roles/discoveryengine.agentspaceUser (project-level, or per-app with agentspaceRestrictedUser at project level) plus a Gemini Enterprise license (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/access-control)
Creating agents in Agent Gallery / Workflow Builder requires a Gemini Enterprise license (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/access-control)

Only roles/discoveryengine.agentspaceAdmin holds discoveryengine.agents.setIamPolicy, while agentspaceUser can only propose agent IAM changes (agentIamProposals) (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/access-control)

Registering an ADK agent in Gemini Enterprise requires Gemini Enterprise Admin (roles/discoveryengine.agentspaceAdmin), the Discovery Engine API enabled and an existing app (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/register-and-manage-an-adk-agent)
An ADK agent registered in Gemini Enterprise must be hosted on Agent Runtime in a matching location (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/register-and-manage-an-adk-agent)

Each Gemini Enterprise agent registration consumes the daily agent-creation quota, which scales with distributed licenses (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/register-and-manage-an-adk-agent)

Gemini Enterprise admins get roles/discoveryengine.agentspaceAdmin plus Service Usage Consumer and Logs Viewer, typically granted by a project owner (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/access-control)
Distributing Gemini Enterprise licenses needs roles/billing.admin on the Cloud Billing account (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/licenses)
The Discovery Engine service agent needs roles/discoveryengine.serviceAgent on the project for Gemini Enterprise app creation (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/access-control)

If the Discovery Engine service agent lacks roles/discoveryengine.serviceAgent, Gemini Enterprise app creation fails with "Internal error encountered (Code 13)" (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/access-control)
Gemini Enterprise app-level IAM policies are GA since 2026-02-02 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/release-notes)

Gemini Enterprise introduced granular resource-level Admin, Viewer and User roles for apps and data stores on 2026-09-28 and supports custom IAM roles for AI developer tools since 2026-08-18 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/release-notes)

Gemini Enterprise agent sharing is GA since 2026-02-23 (direct, Google Groups, Workforce Identity Federation pools, configurable admin review) (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/release-notes)
Only Gemini Enterprise Admins can transfer ownership of shared agents (since 2026-09-21) (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/release-notes)

Users request Google Cloud Marketplace agents from the Gemini Enterprise Agent Gallery and an administrator reviews them; approved agents appear under "From your organization" (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/agent-gallery.md.txt)
Gemini Enterprise Frontline users can only use agents an admin provisions and cannot create custom skills (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/editions)

Gemini Enterprise Agent Designer (GA 2026-01-12) was renamed Workflow Builder at its GA on 2026-09-03, with an enhanced Agent Gallery (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/release-notes)
Signing in to Gemini Notebook Enterprise requires roles/discoveryengine.notebookLmUser (Cloud NotebookLM User) (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/notebooklm-enterprise/docs/overview)

roles/discoveryengine.notebookLmOwner (Cloud NotebookLM Admin) is the admin role for Gemini Notebook Enterprise, alongside UI-granted roles/discoveryengine.notebookOwner, notebookEditor and notebookViewer (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/notebooklm-enterprise/docs/overview)

In Gemini Notebook Enterprise, roles containing discoveryengine.notebooks.get at project level expose every notebook (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/notebooklm-enterprise/docs/overview)
Optional project-level Gemini API spend caps on the AI Studio Spend page can be set by users with the editor, owner or admin role (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/billing)

Turning the Workspace Gemini app on or off needs the Gemini Settings admin privilege, at Admin console > Generative AI > Gemini app > Service status, scoped by OU or configuration group (group overrides OU) (https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/gemini/turn-the-gemini-app-on-or-off)
The Workspace Gemini app "User access" setting can allow all users regardless of license (https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/gemini/turn-the-gemini-app-on-or-off)

Controlling third-party app access to Workspace data at Admin console > Security > Access and data control > API controls needs the Service Settings admin privilege (https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/apps/control-which-apps-access-google-workspace-data)

Workspace API controls offer per-app levels Trusted, Specific Google data, Limited and Blocked; services can be set Restricted (revoking untrusted tokens); unconfigured third-party apps can be allowed, limited to basic sign-in, or blocked (https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/apps/control-which-apps-access-google-workspace-data)

For Gemini API Unpaid Services, Google uses submitted content and responses to provide, improve and develop products and ML technologies, and human reviewers may read them (disconnected from account, key and project), so sensitive data should not be submitted (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/terms)

Gemini API Paid Services prompts and responses are not used to improve products, are processed under a Data Processing Addendum, and are logged for a limited time only for abuse detection, safety and legal needs (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/terms)
AI Studio counts as Gemini API Paid Services when tied to a billed project or Workspace account (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/billing)

Gemini API users in the EEA, Switzerland or UK get Paid Services data terms on all services, and API clients offered to users there may use only Paid Services; terms effective 2026-03-23, and users must be 18+ (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/terms)
Gemini API Paid Services data may be stored or cached in any country where Google or its agents have facilities (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/terms)
Because Gemini API paid data may be stored anywhere, data residency requires the Cloud platform (Vertex AI) instead of the Gemini API (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/terms)

Gemini Enterprise locations are multi-regions global, us and eu (Google recommends global) plus in-country regions GA with allowlist: Brazil br (2026-10-28), Canada ca, India in, Japan asia-northeast1, Singapore sg, UK europe-west2 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/locations ; https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/release-notes)
Gemini Enterprise regional API hosts are us-discoveryengine.googleapis.com and eu-discoveryengine.googleapis.com (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/locations)

Gemini Enterprise base functionality supports at-rest data residency and ML processing in us, eu and in-country regions, while global has no regional residency (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/locations)

In Gemini Enterprise several models (for example Gemini 4 Carbon, Gemini 3.7 Flash) are global-only, and enabling an unsupported model routes traffic to global (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/locations)
In Gemini Enterprise, Grounding with Google Search is global-only (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/locations)

VPC Service Controls, CMEK (US/EU multi-regions only, not global), Access Transparency and data residency are supported for Gemini Enterprise Standard/Plus and Gemini Notebook Enterprise, except when Grounding with Google Search is enabled (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/compliance-security-controls)

Gemini Enterprise lists HIPAA, FedRAMP, ISO 27001/27017/27018/27701, SOC 1/2/3, PCI DSS and BSI C5:2020 certifications (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/compliance-security-controls)
Antigravity in Gemini Enterprise is excluded from Access Transparency, FedRAMP, IL4/IL5, ISO, ITAR and SOC (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/compliance-security-controls)
Model Armor can screen prompts and responses in Gemini Enterprise apps and Gemini Notebook Enterprise (since 2025-09-15) (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/release-notes)
Model Armor for Gemini Enterprise is not available in the global location (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/locations)
Governance of Gemini Enterprise agents and MCP servers through Agent Registry and Agent Gateway is GA since 2026-06-25 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/release-notes)
Agent Gateway governs Gemini Enterprise agents and MCP servers together with Agent Registry, GA since 2026-06-25 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/release-notes)

Gemini Enterprise custom MCP server data stores are off by default behind an organization policy constraint (2026-04-28), and managed org policy constraints for allowed data sources and egress FQDNs went GA 2026-07-06/07 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/release-notes)

Gemini Enterprise ingestion connectors enforce source ACLs by combining an identity sync (users to groups, every 30 minutes to 7 days) and a full sync (content to groups) (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/connectors/introduction-to-connectors-and-data-stores)

Gemini Enterprise federated connectors query the source live and send the query string to third-party backends (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/connectors/introduction-to-connectors-and-data-stores)

Each Gemini Enterprise document supports up to 3,000 readers, and access control can only be chosen at data store creation (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/configure-identity-provider)
Gemini Enterprise Cloud Storage, BigQuery and custom sources need explicit ACLs or external identity mapping (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/configure-identity-provider)

Gemini Enterprise audit logs appear under protoPayload.serviceName="discoveryengine.googleapis.com": Admin Activity for configuration and IAM changes, and Data Access (must be enabled) for Search, StreamAssist and similar (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/audit-logging)
Gemini Enterprise usage audit logs of user queries and responses in Cloud Logging are GA since 2026-02-04 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/release-notes)
Gemini Enterprise admins can configure the chat retention period (GA 2026-03-11) (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/release-notes)

In Workspace, customer prompts and content are not used to train generative AI models outside the domain without permission, Gemini app and Gemini Notebook chats are not human-reviewed without permission, and Gemini only accesses content the user can already see (https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/gemini/generative-ai-in-google-workspace-privacy-hub)

Most Workspace Business, Enterprise, Essentials, Frontline and Nonprofits editions (and AI Expanded Access) get the Gemini app as a core service with enterprise data protections, while Business Base, Essentials Starter, Cloud Identity, Workspace Individual and others get it as an additional service under consumer terms where chats may be human-reviewed (https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/gemini/turn-the-gemini-app-on-or-off)
Gemini in Workspace prompts are kept 90 days to indefinitely (admin-set) (https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/gemini/generative-ai-in-google-workspace-privacy-hub)
Workspace Gemini app history is kept 3, 18 (default) or 36 months, or up to 72 hours with history off (https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/gemini/turn-the-gemini-app-on-or-off)
Gemini Notebook does not retain prompts after the session (https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/gemini/generative-ai-in-google-workspace-privacy-hub)

Workspace Gemini certifications: SOC 1/2/3, ISO 9001, 27001, 27701, 27017, 27018, 42001, FedRAMP High (Gemini in Workspace apps and Gemini app) and HIPAA (Gemini in Workspace) (https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/gemini/generative-ai-in-google-workspace-privacy-hub)
Gemini Notebook and Gemini in Chrome are not covered by ISO, SOC, FedRAMP or the HIPAA BAA (https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/gemini/generative-ai-in-google-workspace-privacy-hub)

Workspace data regions at Admin console > Data > Compliance > Data regions (Data Regions Settings admin privilege) offer United States, Europe or No preference on qualifying Business/Enterprise/Frontline/Education editions (https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/compliance/choose-a-geographic-location-for-your-data)

The Workspace data regions page does not state Gemini coverage, and Workspace data-region settings do not apply to Gemini Notebook data (https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/compliance/choose-a-geographic-location-for-your-data ; https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/gemini/generative-ai-in-google-workspace-privacy-hub)
Gemini Code Assist Standard and Enterprise both list IP indemnification (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/docs/codeassist/overview)
Gemini Code Assist Enterprise adds IP indemnification plus code customization from GitHub, GitLab and Bitbucket (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/docs/codeassist/overview)

Gemini API prices are USD per 1M input and output tokens (output includes thinking tokens), some media per image or per second/minute, and Grounding with Google Search per 1,000 requests; Flex and Priority tiers exist (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/pricing)
The Gemini Batch API is 50% off standard prices (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/pricing)
Gemini 3.8 Flash costs $0.75 input / $3.75 output per 1M tokens through 2026-12-31 (shown 2026-11-14) (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/pricing)
Gemini 3.8 Flash rises to $1.50 input / $7.50 output per 1M tokens from 2027-01-01 (shown 2026-11-14) (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/pricing)
Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview costs $2.00 input / $12.00 output per 1M tokens with no free tier (shown 2026-11-14) (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/pricing)
Grounding with Google Search for Gemini 3+ includes 5,000 free requests per month, then $14 per 1,000 (shown 2026-11-14) (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/pricing)

Gemini API usage tiers (shown 2026-11-14): Free (no billing); Tier 1 (linked billing, $250 monthly cap); Tier 2 ($100 paid and 3 days since first payment, $2,000 cap); Tier 3 ($1,000 paid and 30 days, $20,000-$100,000+ cap) (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/billing ; https://aistudio.google.com/docs/rate-limits)

Gemini API rate limits are per project and cover RPM, input TPM, RPD (reset midnight Pacific), plus IPM/TPD for some models and a rolling 10-minute spend limit ($10 Tier 1, $200 Tier 2/3); paid tiers can request increases (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/rate-limits)
Exceeding any Gemini API rate limit returns 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/rate-limits)
Gemini API Prepay and Postpay plans exist from 2026-03-23, with new users defaulting to Prepay ($5 minimum, $5,000 maximum, credits expire after 12 months) (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/billing)
On Gemini API Prepay, at a $0 balance all keys in linked projects fail with HTTP 402 (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/billing)
Google Cloud accounts opened after 2026-03-02 cannot use the $300 Welcome credit for Gemini API or AI Studio (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/billing)

Gemini Enterprise Business, Standard, Plus and Frontline are seat subscriptions, while the Pay-as-you-go edition and "Pay-as-you-go usage above quota" (renamed from "Overages" 2026-10-06) bill usage (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/editions ; https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/release-notes)

Partner models Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5 are pay-as-you-go in Gemini Enterprise, and seat credits cover only first-party Gemini models (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/editions)
Claude Sonnet 5.5 is a pay-as-you-go partner model in Gemini Enterprise not covered by seat credits (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/editions)

The official Gemini Enterprise pricing URL https://cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise/pricing returned 404 on 2026-11-14 (secondary) (https://dupple.com/learn/gemini-enterprise-pricing)

Jules usage limits: Base 15 tasks per rolling 24 hours and 3 concurrent; Pro 100 and 15; Ultra 300 and 60 (https://jules.google/docs/usage-limits)

The Gemini API is a Google AI offering documented at https://aistudio.google.com/docs (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/models)

Gemini API docs URLs https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/* now return HTTP 301 to https://aistudio.google.com/docs/* (for example /gemini-api/docs/models goes to https://aistudio.google.com/docs/models) (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/models)
Gemini API model gemini-4-argon is part of the Gemini 4 frontier tier and went GA 2026-10-13 (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/changelog ; https://aistudio.google.com/docs/models)
Gemini API model gemini-4-carbon went GA 2026-11-10 (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/changelog ; https://aistudio.google.com/docs/models)
Gemini API model gemini-4-hydrogen went GA 2026-11-12 (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/changelog ; https://aistudio.google.com/docs/models)

gemini-4-hydrogen has a 1,048,576-token context window shared by input and output and 65,536-token default synchronous output (up to 1,048,576 with long decode), with thinking levels low/medium/high/xhigh (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/models/gemini-4-hydrogen.md)

gemini-4-hydrogen supports function calling, code execution, computer use, File Search, URL context, Search and Maps grounding, and structured outputs (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/models/gemini-4-hydrogen.md)
gemini-4-hydrogen does not support the Live API, audio or image generation, or explicit caching (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/models/gemini-4-hydrogen.md)
gemini-3.8-flash is a stable Gemini API workhorse model, GA 2026-09-02 (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/models ; https://aistudio.google.com/docs/changelog)
gemini-3.6-flash is a stable Gemini API model, GA 2026-07-21 (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/models ; https://aistudio.google.com/docs/changelog)
gemini-3.5-flash-lite is a stable Gemini API model, GA 2026-07-21 (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/models ; https://aistudio.google.com/docs/changelog)
gemini-3.1-flash-lite is a stable Gemini API model, GA 2026-05-07 (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/models ; https://aistudio.google.com/docs/changelog)
gemini-3-flash-preview is still listed as a preview Gemini API model (as of 2026-11-14) (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/models)
gemini-3.1-pro-preview is still listed as a preview Gemini API model (as of 2026-11-14) (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/models)
On 2026-10-08 gemini-3.7-flash was replaced by gemini-3.8-flash (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/changelog)
On 2026-10-08 gemini-3.5-flash began routing to gemini-3.6-flash (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/changelog)
gemini-3-pro-preview was shut down on 2026-03-09 and now points to gemini-3.1-pro-preview (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/changelog)

gemini-2.5-pro is deprecated with API access limited to existing users, and on 2026-12-01 it routes to gemini-3.8-flash (billed at 3.8 Flash rates) (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/deprecations.md ; https://aistudio.google.com/docs/models)

gemini-2.5-flash is deprecated with API access limited to existing users, and on 2026-12-01 it routes to gemini-3.5-flash-lite (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/deprecations.md ; https://aistudio.google.com/docs/models)
gemini-2.5-flash-lite is served until further notice (as of 2026-11-14) (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/deprecations.md)
gemini-2.0-flash, gemini-2.0-flash-001, gemini-2.0-flash-lite and gemini-2.0-flash-lite-001 were shut down on 2026-06-01 (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/changelog)

Current Gemini Live API models are gemini-3.8-live and gemini-3.8-live-extended-thinking (GA 2026-09-15) and gemini-3.5-live-translate-preview, while gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview is legacy (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/models)
gemini-2.5-flash-native-audio-preview-12-2025 shuts down 2027-03-31, with replacement gemini-3.8-live (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/deprecations.md)

The Gemini Live API is a stateful WebSocket (WSS) API taking 16-bit PCM audio at 16 kHz, JPEG images at up to 1 FPS and text, and outputting 16-bit PCM audio at 24 kHz (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/live.md)
The Gemini Live API supports 70 languages and its tools are function calling and Google Search (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/live.md)

Gemini TTS models gemini-3.8-flash-tts and gemini-3.8-flash-lite-tts went GA 2026-09-22; STT models are gemini-3.5-transcribe and gemini-3.5-transcribe-live (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/models ; https://aistudio.google.com/docs/changelog)

Gemini image model gemini-nano-banana-2.1 went GA 2026-10-06; other image models are gemini-3.1-flash-image, gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image and gemini-3-pro-image (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/models ; https://aistudio.google.com/docs/changelog)
Gemini video model gemini-omni-1.2-flash went GA 2026-11-05 (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/models ; https://aistudio.google.com/docs/changelog)
The Gemini API music model is lyria-3.5 (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/models)
Imagen 4 was shut down on 2026-08-17 (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/changelog)
gemini-embedding-2 is a multimodal Gemini embedding model, GA 2026-04-22 (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/changelog)
gemini-embedding-001 (text) has a shutdown date of 2028-05-14 (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/deprecations.md)
text-embedding-004 was shut down 2026-01-14 (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/changelog)
gemini-embedding-2-preview routes to gemini-embedding-2 since 2026-11-06 (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/changelog)

The Interactions API is POST https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/interactions (client.interactions.create) and went GA in June 2026 as the default Gemini API interface (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/interactions-overview.md)

The Interactions API adds server-side state (previous_interaction_id), store (default true; retention 55 days paid, 1 day free), background=true for long tasks, and observable steps (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/interactions-overview.md)
The Interactions API is the default Gemini API interface and generateContent is labelled legacy but still supported (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/interactions-overview.md)

The Interactions API does not yet support Batch API, Python automatic function calling or explicit caching (those remain on generateContent), and tools, system instructions and generation config must be re-sent each turn (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/interactions-overview.md)

The Interactions API response schema moved from outputs to steps and response_format changed; the new schema became the default on 2026-05-26 and the legacy schema was removed on 2026-06-08 (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/changelog)
In the Interactions API total_reasoning_tokens was renamed total_thought_tokens on 2025-12-19 (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/changelog)
Gemini API Managed Agents has been in public preview since 2026-05-19 (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/agents.md)

Gemini API Managed Agents is a configurable agent harness where one API call provisions an Ubuntu sandbox (Python 3.12, Node.js 22) in which the agent reasons, runs code, manages files and browses (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/agents.md)
The Antigravity agent (antigravity-preview-09-2026) is offered through Gemini API Managed Agents (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/agents.md ; https://aistudio.google.com/docs/models)

Deep Research (deep-research-preview-04-2026, deep-research-max-preview-04-2026) is offered through Gemini API Managed Agents (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/agents.md ; https://aistudio.google.com/docs/models)
Gemini API Managed Agents allows up to 1,000 managed agents per project, and environments are permanently deleted after 7 days of inactivity (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/agents.md)

Gemini API Managed Agents environments allow unrestricted outbound network by default, a network allowlist can restrict it, and secrets are stored as managed credentials that the egress proxy injects at request time (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/agents.md)
Gemini API Managed Agents compute is not billed during preview (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/agents.md)

Gemini API tool_choice accepts auto (default), any, none and validated; allowed_tools restricts any to a subset; parallel and compositional (chained) calls are supported (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/function-calling.md)
Google recommends at most 10 to 20 active tools for Gemini function calling (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/function-calling.md)

Gemini 4 and Gemini 3 series models can combine built-in tools (Google Search, Google Maps, code execution, URL context, File Search) with custom function calls in one turn, a preview added 2026-03-18; structured outputs with tools is also preview (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/tools.md ; https://aistudio.google.com/docs/changelog)

The Gemini API google_search tool (google_search_retrieval on older models) returns google_search_call and google_search_result steps and url_citation annotations, and combines with code execution, URL context and Maps grounding (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/google-search.md)
Apps using Grounding with Google Search must render the search_suggestions HTML (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/google-search.md)
The Gemini API url_context tool ({"type": "url_context"}) accepts up to 20 URLs per request and 34 MB per URL (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/url-context.md)
The Gemini url_context tool cannot read paywalled content, YouTube, Google Workspace files, or video and audio files (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/url-context.md)

The Gemini API code_execution tool runs Python only with a 30-second maximum runtime and up to 5 automatic regenerations on error; custom packages cannot be installed and only matplotlib renders graphs (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/code-execution.md)
The Gemini code_execution tool has no extra charge beyond tokens (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/code-execution.md)

The Gemini API computer_use tool is GA since 2026-10-30 and works with environment browser, mobile or desktop on gemini-4-*, gemini-3.8-flash, gemini-3.5-flash-lite and gemini-3-flash-preview (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/computer-use.md ; https://aistudio.google.com/docs/changelog)
The older gemini-2.5-computer-use-preview-10-2025 computer use model is shut down (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/models)

Gemini Computer Use responses can carry safety_decision: require_confirmation, and the client must then get user approval and send safety_acknowledgement in the function_result; coordinates are normalized to 0 to 999 (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/computer-use.md)
Gemini Computer Use enable_prompt_injection_detection (default false; Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite or later) scans screenshots (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/computer-use.md)

Gemini API File Search (managed RAG) launched in public preview on 2025-11-06 and added multimodal search on 2026-05-05 (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/file-search.md ; https://aistudio.google.com/docs/changelog)

Gemini File Search uses fileSearchStores and fileSearchStores.documents resources, with uploadToFileSearchStore or importFile for ingestion and metadata_filter for search (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/file-search.md)
Gemini File Search image search (PNG or JPEG) requires gemini-embedding-2 (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/file-search.md)
Gemini File Search charges for embeddings at indexing time; storage and query-time embeddings are free, and retrieved tokens are billed as context (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/file-search.md)

Gemini File Search allows 100 MB per document, recommends under 20 GB per store, and caps total storage per project at 1 GB (Free), 10 GB (Tier 1), 100 GB (Tier 2) or 1 TB (Tier 3) (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/file-search.md)
Gemini File Search is not usable in the Live API and cannot be combined with Google Search or URL context (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/file-search.md)

Gemini API implicit caching is on by default for Gemini 2.5 and newer, with a minimum of 4,096 tokens for Gemini 4, 3.8 Flash, 3.6 Flash and 3.1 Pro Preview and 2,048 for 2.5 models (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/caching.md)

Gemini explicit caching (/v1beta/cachedContents) works only on Gemini 3 and 2.5 through generateContent, not on Gemini 4 and not in the Interactions API (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/caching.md ; https://aistudio.google.com/api-reference.md)
The Gemini Batch API (/v1beta/batches) costs 50% of standard and targets 24-hour turnaround (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/batch-api.md)
The Gemini Batch API takes inline requests (under 20 MB total) or JSONL input files (up to 2 GB) and expires jobs pending or running over 48 hours (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/batch-api.md)
The Gemini Batch API is generateContent-only and supports batch embeddings through batches.create_embeddings (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/batch-api.md)

A2A protocol v1.0.0 is the current spec (after 0.3.0, 0.2.6 and 0.1.0) and has JSON-RPC, gRPC and HTTP+JSON/REST bindings (https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/specification/)

A2A v1.0 core operations are SendMessage, SendStreamingMessage, GetTask, ListTasks, CancelTask, SubscribeToTask, push notification config CRUD and GetExtendedAgentCard (https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/specification/)
The A2A Agent Card lives at https://{domain}/.well-known/agent-card.json (https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/specification/)

A2A v1.0 breaking changes: methods renamed (message/send to SendMessage), unified Part without kind (mimeType became mediaType), uppercase enums (TASK_STATE_COMPLETED), Agent Card url, preferredTransport and additionalInterfaces became supportedInterfaces[], cursor-based pagination, and implicit and password OAuth flows removed (https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/whats-new-v1/)
A2A clients without an A2A-Version header are treated as 0.3 (https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/whats-new-v1/ ; https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/specification/)
A2A is a Linux Foundation project (Apache 2.0, GitHub org a2aproject) (https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/community/)
A banner dated 2026-08-27 announces that A2A joined the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) (https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/)

A2A SDKs are Python a2a-sdk, Go github.com/a2aproject/a2a-go/v2, Java org.a2aproject.sdk:a2a-java-sdk-reference-jsonrpc, JS @a2a-js/sdk, .NET A2A, and Rust a2a-lf / a2a-server-lf (https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/)
