An OCI tenancy is the root compartment that holds all of an organization's OCI resources; Oracle creates it at sign-up, and users, groups, dynamic groups and federation providers are managed at tenancy level (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Identity/Concepts/overview.htm).

OCI compartments are logical (not physical) groupings for access control, billing and isolation, and subcompartments can form hierarchies six levels deep (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/Content/Identity/Tasks/managingcompartments.htm).
A child OCI compartment inherits policies from its parents (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Identity/Concepts/overview.htm).

IAM resources are global but their master definitions live in the tenancy's home region, so IAM changes must be made there and propagate to other regions (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Identity/Concepts/overview.htm).

A tenancy lives in exactly one realm and can access only regions in it: commercial OC1 (45 commercial regions listed), separate government realms (US Government Cloud, US Defense Cloud, UK Sovereign Cloud, Australia Government and Defence) and dedicated realms; the Generative AI region page also names OC2 (US Gov), OC3 (US DoD), OC4 (UK Gov) and OC19 (EU Sovereign) (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/General/Concepts/regions.htm ; https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/model-endpoint-regions.htm).

Trial, Free Tier and Pay As You Go tenancies can subscribe to one region (PAYG can request more through a Subscribed region count limit increase), while Universal Credit tenancies can subscribe to all public commercial regions (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/General/Concepts/regions.htm).

Oracle's OCI billing models are Annual Universal Credits, Monthly Universal Credit (subject to Oracle approval), Universal Credits Pay As You Go, BYOL, Oracle Cloud at Customer and Government Subscriptions (https://docs.oracle.com/get-started/subscriptions-cloud/ocpib/billing-models-offered.html).

The Oracle Cloud Free Tier combines Always Free services with a 30-day trial of US$300 in credits (select countries) (secondary: search summary of the Oracle page) (https://www.oracle.com/cloud/free/).
Signing up for the Oracle Cloud Free Tier requires a credit card, and only one free account is allowed per person (secondary: search summary of the Oracle page) (https://www.oracle.com/cloud/free/).

Oracle Database@AWS is bought through an AWS Marketplace private offer (or a public offer): you request a private offer from the AWS console, Oracle sales negotiates it, you accept it in AWS Marketplace, and onboarding links the AWS account to a new or existing OCI tenancy; Autonomous Database Serverless also has a public offer (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/database-at-aws/oaaws-task-2-request-offer.htm ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/odb/latest/UserGuide/setting-up.html).

Oracle Database@Azure is bought by accepting a private offer in Azure Marketplace under Private Offer Management, then linking or creating an OCI tenancy (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/oracle/oracle-db/onboard-oracle-database).

Oracle Database@AWS onboarding creates the base compartment MulticloudLink_AWS_<YYYYMMDDHHMMSS> and the policies MulticloudLink_AWS_Management, MulticloudLink_AWS_<UNIQUE_ID>_User_Group_Policies, ..._Observability and ..._Tenant_Level, and the docs say not to change or delete them (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/Content/database-at-aws/oaaws-rbac.htm).

Day-one asks for a client engagement (derived from the policy pages): the tenancy OCID, home region and subscribed regions; a user in the right identity domain with that domain's name; membership in a group with a compartment-scoped policy; a sandbox compartment OCID; the dynamic groups or resource-principal policies the agent runtime needs; and VCN, subnet and private endpoint details if public endpoints are blocked (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/iam-policies.htm ; https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai-agents/iam-policies.htm).

A client engagement should ask for membership in a group with a compartment-scoped policy such as manage generative-ai-family in the project compartment (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/iam-policies.htm).

A client engagement should ask for a compartment-scoped policy such as manage genai-agent-family in the project compartment (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai-agents/iam-policies.htm).
Agent runtimes on OCI need dynamic groups or resource-principal policies, which should be requested on day one (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai-agents/iam-policies.htm).
OCI IAM uses identity domains, and each tenancy has a Default identity domain in the root compartment (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Identity/home.htm).

Identity domains provide authentication, SSO and identity lifecycle for OCI, Oracle SaaS and non-Oracle apps, and the domain types you can create depend on your subscription (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Identity/home.htm).

There are six identity domain types: Free (2,000 users, 2 non-Oracle apps), Oracle Apps (1,000,000 users, 2 non-Oracle apps), Oracle Apps Premium (hybrid IAM for Oracle enterprise apps), Premium (full feature set, 5,000 non-Oracle apps, App Gateway for any app), External User (billed per stored user) and External Active User (billed per monthly active user) (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Identity/sku/overview.htm).
The Free identity domain type allows 2,000 users and 2 non-Oracle apps (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Identity/sku/overview.htm).
The Oracle Apps identity domain type allows 1,000,000 users and 2 non-Oracle apps (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Identity/sku/overview.htm).
The Premium identity domain type has the full feature set, 5,000 non-Oracle apps and App Gateway for any app (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Identity/sku/overview.htm).

External identity domains have no dynamic groups and no OCI resource management, and the Default domain can't be changed to an External type (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Identity/sku/overview.htm).

Human SSO uses SAML 2.0 federation into an identity domain: you can add SAML 2.0 identity providers and export the domain's SAML metadata (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Identity/home.htm).
OCI identity domains support OIDC for compliant applications (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Identity/home.htm).
Apple became a supported social IdP for OCI identity domains on 2025-11-05 (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/services/identity/).

The seeded sign-on policy Security Policy for OCI Console has rules for MFA for administrators and for all users, and is active by default in new tenancies (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Security/Reference/iam_security_topic-iam_mfa_with_identity_domains.htm).

The Console MFA sign-on policy is not auto-activated if the default sign-on policy was modified or the tenancy is federated (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/Content/Identity/signonpolicies/managingsignonpolicies.htm).

Per OCI user: 3 API signing keys, 2 auth tokens (which do not expire), 2 Customer Secret keys (S3 compatibility), 2 SMTP credentials and 10 OAuth 2.0 client credentials (up to 10 scopes each; the limit can be raised), plus IAM database passwords (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/Content/Identity/Tasks/managingcredentials.htm).

API signing keys are the default SDK and CLI credential, and the SDK config file ~/.oci/config holds user, fingerprint, tenancy, region and key_file (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/API/Concepts/sdk_authentication_methods.htm).

oci setup config creates the ~/.oci/config API signing key configuration, and oci setup bootstrap does it with a browser-based flow (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/API/Concepts/sdk_authentication_methods.htm).
Oracle advises using API signing keys only where storing private keys locally is acceptable (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/API/Concepts/sdk_authentication_methods.htm).
oci session authenticate creates a browser-based session token that expires after 60 minutes by default (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/API/Concepts/sdk_authentication_methods.htm).
Session token authentication is not supported in the PowerShell or Ruby SDKs (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/API/Concepts/sdk_authentication_methods.htm).

Auth tokens are Oracle-generated strings for third-party APIs that don't support OCI request signing, for example Swift or OCIR docker login (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/Content/Identity/Tasks/managingcredentials.htm).
OCI auth tokens never expire and can't be chosen or changed (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/Content/Identity/Tasks/managingcredentials.htm).

IAM user OAuth 2.0 client credentials call https://auth.<oci_region>.oraclecloud.com/oauth2/token with grant_type=client_credentials&scope=<audience>-<scope> (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/Content/Identity/Tasks/managingcredentials.htm).
OAuth 2.0 client credential access tokens expire after 3600 seconds, and regenerating the secret invalidates the old one (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/Content/Identity/Tasks/managingcredentials.htm).

Instance principals let compute instances call OCI without stored credentials: OCI issues instance certificates and rotates them several times a day, and instances are granted access through dynamic groups (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Identity/Tasks/callingservicesfrominstances.htm).

Use instance principals with oci ... --auth instance_principal or OCI_CLI_AUTH=instance_principal, Python oci.auth.signers.InstancePrincipalsSecurityTokenSigner(), or Terraform auth = "InstancePrincipal" (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Identity/Tasks/callingservicesfrominstances.htm).
Terraform authenticates as an instance principal with auth = "InstancePrincipal" (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Identity/Tasks/callingservicesfrominstances.htm).
Every instance principal gets compartment_inspect, which can't be revoked (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Identity/Tasks/callingservicesfrominstances.htm).

Resource principals cover non-instance resources (OCI Functions, Generative AI Agents, data ingestion jobs and hosted applications) with a Resource Principal Session Token (RPST), a JWT with res_tenant and res_compartment claims (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Functions/Tasks/functionsaccessingociresources.htm).

OCI Functions authenticate with resource principals; the token is cached for 15 minutes, so policy changes can take that long to apply (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Functions/Tasks/functionsaccessingociresources.htm).

Generative AI Agents and data ingestion jobs authenticate with a Resource Principal Session Token (RPST) (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Functions/Tasks/functionsaccessingociresources.htm).

Python uses oci.auth.signers.get_resource_principals_signer() for resource principals, and the env vars are OCI_RESOURCE_PRINCIPAL_RPST and OCI_RESOURCE_PRINCIPAL_PRIVATE_PEM (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Functions/Tasks/functionsaccessingociresources.htm).

OCI Kubernetes Engine workload identity works only on enhanced clusters and only through an OCI SDK (not the Console or API) (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/ContEng/Tasks/contenggrantingworkloadaccesstoresources.htm).
OKE Workload Identity cannot be used with dynamic groups (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/ContEng/Tasks/contenggrantingworkloadaccesstoresources.htm).

OKE Workload Identity minimum SDKs: Go v65.32.0, Java v2.93.0 / v3.88.0, Python v2.111.0, .NET v87.3.0, Ruby v2.19.0 (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/ContEng/Tasks/contenggrantingworkloadaccesstoresources.htm).

OKE Workload Identity policy syntax is Allow any-user to <verb> <resource> in <location> where all {request.principal.type = 'workload', request.principal.namespace = '<ns>', request.principal.service_account = '<sa>', request.principal.cluster_id = '<cluster-ocid>'} (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/ContEng/Tasks/contenggrantingworkloadaccesstoresources.htm).

Since 2025-07-17, a JWT from an external IdP can be exchanged for a short-lived User Principal Session Token by POST to https://<domainURL>/oauth2/v1/token with grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange, requested_token_type=urn:oci:token-type:oci-upst, subject_token_type=jwt and public_key (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Identity/api-getstarted/json_web_token_exchange.htm ; https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/identity/identity-jwt-to-upst-token-exchange.htm).

The JWT-to-UPST exchange needs an Identity Propagation Trust (/admin/v1/IdentityPropagationTrusts) plus a confidential app's client credentials (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Identity/api-getstarted/json_web_token_exchange.htm).

With allowImpersonation: true, the UPST is issued for a mapped identity-domain service user, which has no password or API keys, and the original subject is recorded in source_authn_prin (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Identity/api-getstarted/json_web_token_exchange.htm).
IAM released JWT-to-RPST token exchange for workload identity federation on 2026-08-26 (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/services/identity/).

External JWTs (GitHub Actions, Kubernetes, other clouds) are exchanged with requested_token_type=urn:oci:token-type:oci-rpst for ephemeral RPSTs, and claimPropagations copies selected claims, prefixed ext_, into the token for policy evaluation; Oracle frames this as 'zero-footprint access for external workloads and AI agents' (secondary for claim details) (https://blogs.oracle.com/cloud-infrastructure/wif-with-ephemeral-rpst ; https://www.ateam-oracle.com/github-actions-oci-a-guide-to-secure-oidc-token-exchange).

Identity domains support ID-JAG cross-domain token exchange since 2026-10-09: OCI IAM cross-app access exchanges a user ID token for an Identity Assertion JWT Authorization Grant (urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id-jag) and redeems it at a target identity domain (secondary for details) (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/services/identity/ ; https://blogs.oracle.com/cloud-infrastructure/?p=18791).
OCI ID-JAG cross-app access also accepts ID-JAGs from trusted external IdPs such as Okta (secondary for details) (https://blogs.oracle.com/cloud-infrastructure/?p=18791).
Identity domains added OAuth resource indicators on 2026-10-07 and Client ID Metadata Document support for OAuth clients on 2026-09-23 (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/services/identity/).
Since 2026-04-23, client secrets of Oracle-provisioned applications are no longer visible (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/services/identity/).

OCI Generative AI API keys are bearer secrets created in the Generative AI service (not IAM signing keys); each key has up to two secrets with their own expirations, shown only once, and can be set active, inactive or revoked with SetApiKeyState (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/api-keys.htm).
The default limit is 100 Generative AI API keys per tenancy (limit name api-key-count) (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/api-keys.htm).

Callers send Authorization: Bearer <secret> to https://inference.generativeai.<region>.oci.oraclecloud.com/20231130/actions/v1/chat/completions or .../responses; API keys launched 2026-01-21 (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/api-keys.htm ; https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/services/generative-ai/).

Oracle positions Generative AI API keys for testing and early development and recommends OCI IAM signed requests for production, for workloads on OCI Functions or OKE, and to avoid long-lived keys (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/get-started-agents.htm).

The oci-genai-auth package provides OciSessionAuth, OciUserPrincipalAuth, OciInstancePrincipalAuth and OciResourcePrincipalAuth as httpx auth for the OpenAI SDK, with api_key="not-used", base URL https://inference.generativeai.<region>.oci.oraclecloud.com/openai/v1 and project=<generativeaiproject OCID> (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/get-started-agents.htm).

The OpenAI-compatible OCI Generative AI base URL is https://inference.generativeai.<region>.oci.oraclecloud.com/openai/v1 (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/get-started-agents.htm).

Hosted agentic applications accept four inbound auth modes: identity domain bearer tokens (OAuth confidential app with client credentials grant, primary audience and scopes), identity domain browser sessions (OAuth 2.1 Authorization Code with PKCE; GA 2026-10-07), OCI IAM request signatures (2026-07-15), or 'No authentication' (2026-10-21; the app must enforce its own access control) (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/governance.htm ; https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/app-authentication.htm).
Identity domain browser-session auth for hosted applications uses OAuth 2.1 Authorization Code with PKCE and went GA on 2026-10-07 (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/services/generative-ai/).
Hosted applications accept OCI IAM request signatures since 2026-07-15 (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/services/generative-ai/).
The 'No authentication' mode for hosted applications (2026-10-21) means the app must enforce its own access control (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/app-authentication.htm).

The 'Permissions to Generative AI Resources' page says 'OAuth is the only supported authentication type for agentic tasks', while the newer get-started-agents page documents both API keys and IAM signing for the Responses API, so the OAuth-only statement likely applies to hosted applications (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/access.htm ; https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/get-started-agents.htm).

Autonomous Database accepts IAM database tokens once enabled with DBMS_CLOUD_ADMIN.ENABLE_EXTERNAL_AUTHENTICATION(type => 'OCI_IAM') (add force => TRUE if another external auth is enabled) (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/autonomous-database-serverless/doc/enable-iam-authentication.html).

oci iam db-token get fetches an Autonomous Database IAM token (also with --auth security_token or --auth instance_principal) (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/autonomous-database-serverless/doc/iam-access-database.html).

IAM token clients need TCPS, SSL_SERVER_DN_MATCH=ON and TOKEN_AUTH=OCI_TOKEN, and 19c clients must be at least 19.16 (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/autonomous-database-serverless/doc/iam-access-database.html).

A Generative AI Agents agent acts as a resource principal (request.principal.type='genaiagent', dynamic group resource.type='genaiagent'), and Generative AI API keys appear as request.principal.type='generativeaiapikey' (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai-agents/iam-policies.htm).

OCI has no dedicated 'agent identity' principal type: agents use existing principal types, and the IAM release notes for 2025-11 to 2026-11 announce no agent-specific identity type (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/services/identity/).

OCI IAM policy grammar is Allow <subject> to <verb> <resource-type> in <tenancy | compartment <name>> [where <conditions>], with subjects group, dynamic-group, any-user or any-group and cumulative verbs inspect < read < use < manage (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/Content/Identity/policieshow/Policy_Basics.htm).

Groups outside the Default domain must be domain-qualified in policies: group <identity_domain_name>/<group_name>, or with quotes for dynamic groups, for example dynamic-group '<idcs-domain-name>/<dynamic-group-name>' (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/Content/Identity/policieshow/Policy_Basics.htm ; https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai-agents/iam-policies.htm).

The Administrators group policy Allow group Administrators to manage all-resources in tenancy can't be changed or deleted, and the group must always have at least one member (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Identity/Concepts/overview.htm).

IAM deny policies went GA on 2025-11-20 with syntax deny <subject> to <verb> <resource> in <scope> [where ...] (also deny admit and deny endorse), and deny overrides allow (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/identity/deny-policies.htm).
Only the default domain's Administrators group can enable deny policies, and that group is always exempt (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/Content/Identity/policysyntax/denypolicies.htm).

Enabling deny policies creates a root policy restricting who manages deny statements and can't be turned off; the Policy Basics page still says 'Policies only allow access', which predates this feature (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/Content/Identity/policysyntax/denypolicies.htm).

Cross-tenancy access uses paired endorse and admit statements, for example an admit in the resource tenancy granting use database-connections must match an endorse in the user's tenancy (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/autonomous-database-serverless/doc/iam-access-database-cross-tenancy.html).

generative-ai-response, generative-ai-semantic-store and generative-ai-nl2sql are used in the agents quick start but are not in the generative-ai-family list on the IAM page (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/get-started-agents.htm).

Vault resource types are vaults, keys, key-delegate, hsm-cluster, secrets, secret-versions and secret-bundles; key-delegate lets integrated services use a key without letting the grantee use it directly, and reading secret content needs read secret-bundles (SECRET_BUNDLE_READ) (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Identity/Reference/keypolicyreference.htm).
The aggregate secret-family covers secrets, secret-versions and secret-bundles (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Identity/Reference/keypolicyreference.htm).

Oracle has a contractual Zero Data Retention agreement with xAI (Grok) for OCI Generative AI (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/data-handling.htm).

Cohere, Meta Llama and OpenAI gpt-oss requests stay in OCI, while Gemini and Grok requests go to Google or xAI locations: Gemini in US regions uses Google Americas, Frankfurt uses Google EU, and Osaka or Hyderabad may process globally (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/data-handling.htm ; https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/model-endpoint-regions.htm).

OCI Generative AI Agents does not use knowledge bases or chat data for training, does not retain chat data beyond the session, and stores managed knowledge base data isolated per customer (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai-agents/data-handling.htm).

A service gateway lets VCN resources in private subnets reach Oracle Services Network services (for example Object Storage) in the same region without an internet or NAT gateway, using the CIDR labels All <region> Services in Oracle Services Network or OCI <region> Object Storage; IAM network sources can restrict bucket access to a specific VCN (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Network/Tasks/servicegateway.htm).

Autonomous Database has three network access options: secure access from everywhere (public, with optional ACL), access from allowed IPs and VCNs only (ACL required), and private endpoint only (VCN with NSG rules) (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/autonomous-database-serverless/doc/network-access-options.html).

An OCI Generative AI hosted agentic application is an "Application" (autoscaling, managed storage, VCN, endpoint auth) plus a "Deployment" that runs your container image (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/agents.htm).
An OCI Generative AI hosted agent Deployment runs a container image from OCI Container Registry (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/agents.htm).

The OCI Responses API supports four built-in tool types: `file_search` (vector stores), `code_interpreter` (Python in an OCI-managed container), `function` (client-executed) and `mcp` (remote MCP server) (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/responses-api.htm).
The OCI Responses API `mcp` tool type calls a remote MCP server (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/responses-api.htm).
NL2SQL is not configured through the OCI Responses API `tools` parameter (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/responses-api.htm).

The OCI Responses API added xAI tools on 2026-05-29, background mode on 2026-07-29 and compaction via `POST /responses/compact` or `context_management` on 2026-10-27 (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/services/generative-ai).

An OCI Generative AI project groups responses, conversations, files, containers and sandboxes, and sets optional short-term memory compaction and optional long-term memory (an extraction model plus an embedding model) (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/get-started-agents.htm).
OCI Generative AI project response and conversation retention is at most 720 hours (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/get-started-agents.htm).

Neither OCI Generative AI project memory option (short-term compaction or long-term memory) can be disabled after creation without deleting the project (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/agents.htm).
OCI Generative AI sandboxes are available since 2026-10-20 (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/services/generative-ai).

OCI Generative AI sandboxes are temporary Linux workspaces for code and shell commands, scoped to a project and addressable by ID across workflow steps, with managed or custom outbound networking and optional warm pools (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/get-started-agents.htm).
OCI Generative AI sandboxes can't be disabled after you enable them for a project (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/get-started-agents.htm).

OCI Generative AI Enterprise AI NL2SQL generates SQL only, using a "semantic store" with two OCI Database Tools connections: an enrichment connection (higher privilege) and a query connection (lower privilege) (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/get-started-agents.htm).
NL2SQL-generated SQL is executed through the Database Tools MCP Server under the end user's identity (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/get-started-agents.htm).

The OCI Responses API requires a project OCID: pass `project="ocid1.generativeaiproject..."` in the OpenAI SDK, which sends the `OpenAI-Project` header (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/responses-api.htm).
The OCI Responses API `model` parameter is an on-demand model ID, a dedicated endpoint OCID, or a routing profile OCID (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/responses-api.htm).

OCI Generative AI API keys, available since 2026-01-21, are bearer secrets for the OpenAI-compatible endpoints sent as `Authorization: Bearer sk-...` (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/api-keys.htm).

Each OCI Generative AI API key has two secrets with expirations (default three months) and is region-bound; IAM policies match keys with `request.principal.type='generativeaiapikey'` (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/api-keys.htm).
`oci generative-ai api-key create` (or the `CreateApiKey` operation) creates an OCI Generative AI API key (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/api-keys.htm).

`oci-genai-auth` supports instance principal auth via `OciInstancePrincipalAuth` (https://pypi.org/project/oci-genai-auth/).
`oci-genai-auth` supports resource principal auth via `OciResourcePrincipalAuth` (https://pypi.org/project/oci-genai-auth/).
`oci-genai-auth` supports session token auth via `OciSessionAuth` (https://pypi.org/project/oci-genai-auth/).
OCI Generative AI NL2SQL endpoints accept IAM-signed requests only (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/get-started-agents.htm).

NL2SQL semantic store CRUD is at `https://generativeai.${region}.oci.oraclecloud.com/20231130/semanticStores` and Generate SQL is at `https://inference.generativeai.${region}.oci.oraclecloud.com/20260325/semanticStores/{id}/actions/generateSqlFromNl` (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/get-started-agents.htm).

OCI Generative AI agents can call external MCP servers through the Responses API `mcp` tool, which takes `server_label`, `server_url`, `allowed_tools`, `require_approval` and `authorization` (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/mcp.htm).

The Responses API `mcp` tool `authorization` value is a raw token without the `Bearer` prefix, which OCI says it does not store or log (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/mcp.htm).
Only Streamable HTTP is supported for MCP servers called from OCI Generative AI; SSE is deprecated and unsupported (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/get-started-agents.htm).

OCI REST API request signing uses OCI Signature Version 1, based on draft-cavage-http-signatures-08 with `rsa-sha256` and `Authorization: Signature version="1",keyId="<tenancy_ocid>/<user_ocid>/<fingerprint>",...`; GET and DELETE sign `(request-target) host date`, and PUT and POST also sign `x-content-sha256`, `content-type` and `content-length` (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/API/Concepts/signingrequests.htm).
Clock skew over 5 minutes in OCI request signing returns `401 NotAuthenticated` (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/API/Concepts/signingrequests.htm).

`oci raw-request` signs arbitrary REST calls from the OCI CLI and is the Bash sample in the signing docs, alongside Python `oci.signer.Signer`, Java, TypeScript, Go, Ruby and C# samples (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/API/Concepts/signingrequests.htm).

Official OCI SDKs exist for Python (`oci`), Java (`oci-java-sdk`), TypeScript/JavaScript (`oci-sdk`), .NET, Go (`github.com/oracle/oci-go-sdk`), Ruby, and PL/SQL (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/API/Concepts/sdks.htm).
The OCI Python SDK (`oci`) is at v2.191.0, released 2026-11-10 (https://pypi.org/project/oci/).
A PL/SQL OCI SDK is preinstalled in Autonomous AI Database Serverless (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/API/Concepts/sdks.htm).

`langchain-oci` is the LangChain integration for OCI Generative AI, providing `ChatOCIGenAI`, `OCIGenAIEmbeddings`, `OCIGenAIRerank` and `ChatOCIOpenAI` (Responses API), plus a `deepagents` extra with ADB and OpenSearch datastore tools (https://pypi.org/project/langchain-oci/).
`langchain-oci` v0.4.0 is dated 2026-10-21 (https://pypi.org/project/langchain-oci/).

The oracle/mcp GitHub repo is the official collection of local OCI MCP servers, with about 33 servers under `src/` including oci-cloud, oci-api, compute, networking, object-storage, identity, logging, monitoring, usage, pricing, limits, database, db-observability, faaas, registry, resource-search, support, mysql, oracle-data-studio, oracle-db-doc, goldengate and dbtools (https://github.com/oracle/mcp/tree/main/src).
The oracle/mcp README says "This repository is not intended for production use." (https://github.com/oracle/mcp).

`oracle.oci-cloud-mcp-server` is the recommended general-purpose OCI MCP server in oracle/mcp, run with `uvx oracle.oci-cloud-mcp-server@latest` (https://github.com/oracle/mcp/tree/main/src/oci-cloud-mcp-server).

`oracle.oci-cloud-mcp-server` tools are `list_oci_clients`, `find_oci_api`, `describe_oci_operation`, `invoke_oci_api` and `list_client_operations` (SDK-backed) (https://github.com/oracle/mcp/tree/main/src/oci-cloud-mcp-server).

In stdio mode `oracle.oci-cloud-mcp-server` auth uses `OCI_CONFIG_FILE`, `OCI_CONFIG_PROFILE` and `OCI_MCP_AUTH_TYPE` (auto, api_key, security_token, instance_principal, resource_principal, oke_workload_identity and others) (https://github.com/oracle/mcp/tree/main/src/oci-cloud-mcp-server).

In HTTP mode `oracle.oci-cloud-mcp-server` auth uses an IDCS confidential app (`IDCS_DOMAIN`, `IDCS_CLIENT_ID`, scope `oci_mcp.cloud.invoke`) (https://github.com/oracle/mcp/tree/main/src/oci-cloud-mcp-server).

`oracle.oci-api-mcp-server` wraps the OCI CLI, runs with `uvx oracle.oci-api-mcp-server` (stdio only), and has tools `get_oci_command_help` and `run_oci_command` (https://github.com/oracle/mcp/tree/main/src/oci-api-mcp-server).

`oracle.oci-api-mcp-server` blocks `--auth`, `--profile`, `--config-file`, `--endpoint` and `--proxy` overrides and runs with an empty `oci_cli_rc` (https://github.com/oracle/mcp/tree/main/src/oci-api-mcp-server).
`dbtools-mcp-server` in oracle/mcp is a proof of concept as of 2026-11-14 (https://github.com/oracle/mcp/tree/main/src/dbtools-mcp-server).

`dbtools-mcp-server` is a Python FastMCP server with 23 tools (list ADBs, run SQL via Database Tools connections, reports, `ragify_column`, HeatWave and Object Storage) (https://github.com/oracle/mcp/tree/main/src/dbtools-mcp-server).
`dbtools-mcp-server` reads `~/.oci/config` and runs with `python dbtools-mcp-server.py` (stdio) (https://github.com/oracle/mcp/tree/main/src/dbtools-mcp-server).

`oracle-db-doc-mcp-server` searches a locally built index of Oracle Database docs with its single tool `search_oracle_database_documentation` (https://github.com/oracle/mcp/tree/main/src/oracle-db-doc-mcp-server).
A Docker image of `oracle-db-doc-mcp-server` is at `ghcr.io/oracle/mcp/oracle-db-doc` (https://github.com/oracle/mcp/tree/main/src/oracle-db-doc-mcp-server).

The SQLcl MCP server is a local stdio server started with `sql -mcp` that uses SQLcl saved connections (https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/sql-developer-command-line/26.2/sqcug/sqlcl-mcp-server-tools.html).

SQLcl MCP server tools are `list-connections`, `connect`, `disconnect`, `run-sql`, `run-sqlcl` and `schema-information` (https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/sql-developer-command-line/26.2/sqcug/sqlcl-mcp-server-tools.html).

SQLcl MCP restrict levels are set with `-R <0-3>` in the client args (for example `["-R","1","-mcp"]`); the 25.4 docs say the default with no `-R` is level 4, the most restrictive (https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/sql-developer-command-line/25.4/sqcug/configuring-restrict-levels-sqlcl-mcp-server.html).

A later SQLcl changelog says MCP startup now defaults to unrestricted, contradicting the 25.4 docs' level-4 default; that is the newer claim and the version of the change is unconfirmed (https://www.oracle.com/de/tools/sqlcl/sqlcl-changelog.html).

SQLcl MCP logs every request to the `DBTOOLS$MCP_LOG` table in the user's schema, and Oracle advises pruning it regularly (https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/sql-developer-vscode/25.3/sqdnx/monitoring-sqlcl-mcp-server.html).
The Autonomous AI Database MCP Server is a managed remote MCP server, one per database, for 26ai and 19c (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/autonomous-database-serverless/doc/use-mcp-server.html).

The Autonomous AI Database MCP Server is GA, announced in release notes on 2025-12-23 (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/autonomous-database-serverless/2025-12-mcp-server-for-autonomous-ai-database.htm).

The Autonomous AI Database MCP Server endpoint is `https://dataaccess.adb.{region}.oraclecloudapps.com/adb/mcp/v1/databases/{database-ocid}` over Streamable HTTP; a private-endpoint ADB uses a `hostname_prefix` URL reachable only from its VCN (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/autonomous-database-serverless/doc/use-mcp-server.html).

Enable the Autonomous AI Database MCP Server in the Console (database details, then Tool configuration, then Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server, then Edit, then toggle); earlier docs used the free-form tag `adb$feature` = `{"name":"mcp_server","enable":true}` (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/autonomous-database-serverless/doc/use-mcp-server.html).

Autonomous AI Database MCP Server auth options are OAuth dynamic client registration (`GET .../dcr_url` returns a randomized `/r/{random}` URL), static client registration by ADMIN (`POST .../adb/auth/v1/connect/databases/{ocid}/register`), or a bearer token (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/autonomous-database-serverless/doc/use-mcp-server.html).

A bearer token for the Autonomous AI Database MCP Server comes from `POST .../adb/auth/v1/databases/{ocid}/token` (password grant with DB credentials, valid 1 hour) (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/autonomous-database-serverless/doc/use-mcp-server.html).

Autonomous AI Database MCP Server tools are Select AI Agent tools: built-in tools plus custom tools registered with `DBMS_CLOUD_AI_AGENT.CREATE_TOOL` over a PL/SQL function, listed in `USER_AI_AGENT_TOOLS` (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/autonomous-database-serverless/doc/use-mcp-server.html).
Custom Autonomous AI Database MCP tools are registered with `DBMS_CLOUD_AI_AGENT.CREATE_TOOL` (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/autonomous-database-serverless/doc/use-mcp-server.html).
Autonomous AI Database MCP clients see only tools the DB user may use (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/autonomous-database-serverless/doc/use-mcp-server.html).
MLE JavaScript functions can't be Autonomous AI Database MCP tools (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/autonomous-database-serverless/doc/use-mcp-server.html).

The Autonomous AI Database A2A Server publishes Select AI agent teams as A2A agents that clients discover through Agent Cards; it is a built-in, multi-tenant feature for 26ai and 19c on Serverless and Dedicated Region (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/autonomous-database-serverless/doc/agent2agent-protocol.html).
Autonomous AI Database A2A Server auth is OAuth using database credentials (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/autonomous-database-serverless/doc/agent2agent-protocol.html).
The Autonomous AI Database A2A Server is enabled independently of the MCP Server (https://www.oracle.com/autonomous-database/a2a-server/).
The OCI Database Tools MCP Server, a managed MCP server for any Oracle AI Database in OCI, was introduced on 2026-05-12 (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/database-tools/mcp.htm).

OCI Database Tools MCP Server auth is OAuth 2.0 through IAM identity domains (Personal Access Token or token-based), and the runtime identity is Resource Principal or Authenticated Principal (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/database-tools/doc/set-mcp-server.html).

The OCI Database Tools MCP Server exposes toolsets with built-in tools such as `run-sql` and reports, plus custom SQL and PL/SQL tools (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/database-tools/doc/set-mcp-server.html).
Invoking the OCI Database Tools MCP Server uses the IAM policy verb `use database-tools-mcp-servers-invocation` (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/database-tools/doc/set-mcp-server.html).

The Database Tools MCP Server covers Autonomous AI Database, Base Database Service and Exadata Database Service through Database Tools connections at no incremental charge (secondary) (https://www.dbta.com/Editorial/News-Flashes/Enterprise-Grade-Managed-MCP-Servers-in-OCI-Provides-Agentic-Access-to-Any-Oracle-Database-in-the-Cloud-174878.aspx).

The Database Tools MCP Server supports Base Database Service (secondary) (https://www.dbta.com/Editorial/News-Flashes/Enterprise-Grade-Managed-MCP-Servers-in-OCI-Provides-Agentic-Access-to-Any-Oracle-Database-in-the-Cloud-174878.aspx).

The Database Tools MCP Server supports Exadata Database Service (secondary) (https://www.dbta.com/Editorial/News-Flashes/Enterprise-Grade-Managed-MCP-Servers-in-OCI-Provides-Agentic-Access-to-Any-Oracle-Database-in-the-Cloud-174878.aspx).

The Database Tools MCP Server supports Autonomous AI Database, and a later release note added Client ID Metadata Document (CIMD) support (secondary) (https://www.dbta.com/Editorial/News-Flashes/Enterprise-Grade-Managed-MCP-Servers-in-OCI-Provides-Agentic-Access-to-Any-Oracle-Database-in-the-Cloud-174878.aspx).

Oracle Integration exposes one MCP server per project at `https://<instance>.integration.<region>.ocp.oraclecloud.com/mcp-server/v1/projects/<PROJECT_NAME>/mcp`, supporting `tools/list` and `tools/call`, in all OIC regions (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/paas/application-integration/aiagents/faqs-projects-mcp-servers.html).
Oracle Integration MCP server auth is OAuth 2.0 with OCI IAM (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/paas/application-integration/aiagents/faqs-projects-mcp-servers.html).

Calling the Oracle Integration MCP server needs a confidential app with the `ServiceInvoker` role (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/paas/application-integration/aiagents/faqs-projects-mcp-servers.html).

An OIC integration is an MCP tool only if it is in a project and Active, starts with a REST Adapter trigger using OAuth and a JSON payload, uses GET, POST, PUT, DELETE or PATCH, and is registered as an agentic AI tool (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/paas/application-integration/aiagents/faqs-projects-mcp-servers.html).

OIC MCP can be configured in Fusion AI Agent Studio, where Streamable HTTP is recommended (secondary) (https://www.ateam-oracle.com/integrating-fusion-application-ai-agent-studio-with-oic-as-an-external-system).

OIC MCP configuration in AI Agent Studio does not support identity propagation (secondary) (https://www.ateam-oracle.com/integrating-fusion-application-ai-agent-studio-with-oic-as-an-external-system).

Google Gemini calls from OCI Generative AI leave OCI: they are served from Google locations (Americas, EU, Brazil or Asia-Pacific routing by region) (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/agentic-regions.htm).
xAI Grok calls from OCI Generative AI leave OCI because Grok is hosted by xAI (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/model-endpoint-regions.htm).
OCI can reach Google through Oracle Interconnect for Google Cloud in Ashburn and Frankfurt (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/model-endpoint-regions.htm).

On Windows the OCI CLI MSI installer is downloaded from the oci-cli GitHub releases, bundles a compatible Python, and takes precedence over an existing non-MSI install (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/API/SDKDocs/cliinstall.htm).
winget package `Oracle.OCI-CLI` (`winget install --id Oracle.OCI-CLI --exact`) is listed by third-party catalogs (secondary for winget) (https://winstall.app/apps/Oracle.OCI-CLI).

The OCI CLI PowerShell installer: run `Set-ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned`, then `iex ((New-Object System.Net.WebClient).DownloadString('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oracle/oci-cli/master/scripts/install/install.ps1'))`, or download the script and run `./install.ps1 -AcceptAllDefaults`; it installs Python if needed, and offline install is `install.ps1 -OfflineInstall` (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/API/SDKDocs/cliinstall.htm).

Install the OCI CLI via pip with `python -m venv oracle-cli`, `oracle-cli/Scripts/activate`, `pip install oci-cli` (or the release wheel `pip install oci_cli-*-py3-none-any.whl`), and verify with `oci --version` (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/API/SDKDocs/climanualinst.htm).
The current OCI CLI version is 3.96.2, released 2026-11-10 on GitHub (https://github.com/oracle/oci-cli/releases).

`oci setup config` creates an API-key profile via an interactive dialog that generates an RSA key pair and writes the config file; you then upload the public key in the Console, and `oci setup keys` generates keys only (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/API/SDKDocs/cliinstall.htm).

`oci session authenticate` creates a browser-based session token; commands then need `--auth security_token` or `OCI_CLI_AUTH=security_token` (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/API/SDKDocs/clitoken.htm).

OCI session tokens last 1 hour by default and can be refreshed with `oci session refresh --profile

` for up to 24 hours; headless options are `--no-browser` (5 to 60 minutes) and `oci session export` / `oci session import` (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/API/SDKDocs/clitoken.htm).

The OCI config file default path is `~/.oci/config`; on Windows PowerShell it is `$Env:UserProfile\.oci\config` (`C:\Users\<user>\.oci\config`) (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/API/Concepts/sdkconfig.htm).

OCI config file entries are `user`, `fingerprint`, `key_file`, `tenancy` and `region`, plus `security_token_file` for session auth (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/API/Concepts/sdkconfig.htm).

OCI CLI environment variables include `OCI_CLI_CONFIG_FILE`, `OCI_CLI_PROFILE`, `OCI_CLI_AUTH` (`api_key`, `instance_principal`, `resource_principal`, `security_token`, `instance_obo_user`), `OCI_CLI_REGION`, `OCI_CLI_RC_FILE`, `OCI_CLI_KEY_CONTENT` and `OCI_CLI_SECURITY_TOKEN_FILE`; precedence is command option, then env var, then config file (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/API/SDKDocs/clienvironmentvariables.htm).
The OCI CLI accepts `OCI_CLI_AUTH=instance_principal` (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/API/SDKDocs/clienvironmentvariables.htm).
The OCI CLI accepts `OCI_CLI_AUTH=resource_principal` (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/API/SDKDocs/clienvironmentvariables.htm).

OCI CLI command groups for agent work are `generative-ai`, `generative-ai-inference`, `generative-ai-data` (NL2SQL), `generative-ai-sandbox`, `generative-ai-agent`, `generative-ai-agent-runtime`, `db` (includes `db autonomous-database`), `dbtools`, `dbtools-runtime`, `fn`, `api-gateway`, `data-science`, `integration` and `resource-manager` (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/tools/oci-cli/latest/oci_cli_docs/).

The OCI CLI manages OCI Generative AI through the `generative-ai`, `generative-ai-inference`, `generative-ai-data` and `generative-ai-sandbox` command groups (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/tools/oci-cli/latest/oci_cli_docs/).

`oci fn function invoke` is the production invoke path for OCI Functions; it supports `--fn-invoke-type detached` and its sync timeout is `--read-timeout` (default 60 s) (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Functions/Tasks/functionsinvokingfunctions.htm).
The Fn Project CLI `fn invoke` is recommended for development only when invoking OCI Functions (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Functions/Tasks/functionsinvokingfunctions.htm).
The Terraform OCI provider (`oracle/oci`) latest version is v9.13.0, released 2026-11-11 (https://github.com/oracle/terraform-provider-oci/releases).

Recent Terraform OCI provider Generative AI additions are model discovery and routing profiles (v9.3.0, 2026-09-24), GenAI API key support (v9.9.0, 2026-10-06) and bring-your-own reservations for dedicated AI clusters (v9.11.0, 2026-10-21) (https://github.com/oracle/terraform-provider-oci/releases).

The Terraform OCI provider has Gen AI Agents resources such as `oci_generative_ai_agent_agent` (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/tools/terraform-provider-oci/7.23.0/docs/r/generative_ai_agent_agent.html).

OCI Resource Manager is managed Terraform that runs stacks with Plan, Apply, Destroy, Import, Retrieve-latest-providers and Drift-detection jobs, and supports Git, Bitbucket, DevOps and Object Storage sources and private templates (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/ResourceManager/home.htm).

From 2026-04-30, OCI Resource Manager stopped creating stacks or running jobs on Terraform versions earlier than 1.5.x (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/ResourceManager/Reference/terraformversions.htm).

`oci resource-manager stack list-terraform-versions` lists the Terraform versions OCI Resource Manager supports (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/ResourceManager/Tasks/list-tf-versions.htm).
A SQLcl download page lists 26.3.0 (2026-09-29), while the changelog page still shows 26.2.1 (Aug 2026) (https://www.oracle.com/br/database/sqldeveloper/technologies/sqlcl/download/).
SQLcl runs on Java 17 or 21, and later builds also list Java 25 (https://www.oracle.com/de/tools/sqlcl/sqlcl-changelog.html).

The OCI docs root https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/home.htm resolves ("Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Documentation"), and its Develop card links to `devtoolshome.htm` for APIs, SDKs, CLI and Cloud Shell (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/home.htm).

The OCI Generative AI docs home https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/home.htm is the hub for models, Responses API, agents, projects and API keys (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/home.htm).

The OCI Generative AI Agents docs home https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai-agents/home.htm covers the older Agents service, the ADK and the management and client APIs (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai-agents/home.htm).

The OCI API reference and endpoints are at https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/api/ (for example `#/en/generative-ai-inference/`, `#/en/generative-ai-agents/`) (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/api/).
OCI release notes for all services are at https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/releasenotes/index.htm (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/services/generative-ai).
OCI Generative AI release notes are at https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/services/generative-ai (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/services/generative-ai).
OCI Generative AI Agents release notes are at https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/services/generative-ai-agents/ (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/services/generative-ai).
The OCI status page is at https://ocistatus.oraclecloud.com/ (title "OCI Status") (https://ocistatus.oraclecloud.com/).
No `llms.txt` was found for OCI: `https://docs.oracle.com/llms.txt` and `https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/llms.txt` both return 404 as of 2026-11-14 (https://docs.oracle.com/llms.txt).
There is no hosted OCI docs MCP server (https://github.com/oracle/mcp/tree/main/src/oracle-db-doc-mcp-server).
The local `oracle-db-doc-mcp-server` in oracle/mcp indexes Oracle Database docs only, not OCI docs (https://github.com/oracle/mcp/tree/main/src/oracle-db-doc-mcp-server).

Official OCI repos are https://github.com/oracle/mcp (MCP servers), https://github.com/oracle/oci-cli, https://github.com/oracle/terraform-provider-oci and the ADK source under `oci-python-sdk/src/oci/addons/adk` (https://github.com/oracle/mcp).
The oracle/mcp repo of OCI MCP servers is at https://github.com/oracle/mcp (https://github.com/oracle/mcp).

Autonomous AI Database MCP docs start at https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/autonomous-database-serverless/doc/mcp-server.html with prerequisites, use, security and troubleshooting sub-pages (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/autonomous-database-serverless/doc/mcp-server.html).

OCI Generative AI on-demand rate limits are not published; per-tenancy throttling adjusts dynamically to model demand and capacity, and Oracle recommends exponential back-off on rejection (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/dynamic-throttling.htm).

xAI Grok 3 on OCI Generative AI is capped at 100,000 tokens per minute per tenancy, with limit name `grok-3-chat-tokens-per-minute-count` (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/xai-grok-3.htm).

The OCI Responses API is available in nine OC1 regions: `sa-saopaulo-1`, `eu-frankfurt-1`, `ap-hyderabad-1`, `ap-osaka-1`, `me-riyadh-1`, `uk-london-1`, `us-ashburn-1`, `us-chicago-1` and `us-phoenix-1`, and not in UAE East (Dubai) (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/agentic-regions.htm).
xAI models and xAI tools on the OCI Responses API are US-only (Ashburn, Chicago, Phoenix) (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/agentic-regions.htm).
OpenAI gpt-oss on-demand on OCI Generative AI is only in Chicago, Frankfurt and Osaka (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/model-endpoint-regions.htm).
Meta Llama 4 on-demand on OCI Generative AI is Chicago only (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/model-endpoint-regions.htm).
US Gov West, US DoD West and UAE Central (Abu Dhabi) are dedicated-only for OCI Generative AI, with no on-demand (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/model-endpoint-regions.htm).
Use a routing profile from OCI regions without local Generative AI processing (for example Sydney) (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/model-endpoint-regions.htm).
An OCI Generative AI API key must be in the same region as the model and works only for OpenAI-compatible endpoints (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/api-keys.htm).
OCI Generative AI NL2SQL requires IAM auth and does not accept API keys (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/get-started-agents.htm).
OCI Generative AI dedicated-mode model retirement is later than on-demand retirement (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/deprecating-dedicated.htm).
Cohere Embed English 3 retires in OCI Generative AI dedicated mode on 2026-09-30 (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/deprecating-dedicated.htm).
Cohere Embed 4 is the replacement for Cohere Embed English 3 on OCI Generative AI (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai/deprecating-dedicated.htm).
OCI Notifications alert subscribers 14 and 7 days before an OCI Generative AI on-demand model retirement (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/generative-ai/retire-announcements.htm).
Cohere aliases `cohere.command-latest` and `cohere.command-plus-latest` were removed from OCI Generative AI on 2026-07-30 (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/services/generative-ai).
The OCI Generative AI GenerateText API was deprecated effective 2025-05-29 (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/generative-ai/deprecate-api-05292025.htm).
The OCI Generative AI SummarizeText API was deprecated effective 2025-05-29 (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/generative-ai/deprecate-api-05292025.htm).
The OCI Generative AI Chat API replaces the GenerateText API, deprecated effective 2025-05-29 (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/generative-ai/deprecate-api-05292025.htm).
The OCI Generative AI Chat API replaces the SummarizeText API, deprecated effective 2025-05-29 (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/generative-ai/deprecate-api-05292025.htm).

OCI Generative AI Agents (older service) adjustable limit defaults are `agent-count` 2, `knowledge-base-count` 3, `agent-endpoint-per-agent-count` 3 and `session-per-agent-endpoint-count` 1,000 (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai-agents/limits.htm).

OCI Generative AI Agents (older service) fixed limits: tools per agent are 20 in FRA, LHR and ORD but 5 in IAD, GRU and KIX; data source files are 100 MB max; user messages are 24,000 characters max; session idle timeout is 1 hour to 7 days (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai-agents/limits.htm).

OCI Generative AI Agents (older service) regions are `us-ashburn-1`, `sa-saopaulo-1`, `eu-frankfurt-1`, `ap-osaka-1`, `uk-london-1`, `us-chicago-1` and `us-phoenix-1` (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/generative-ai-agents/overview.htm).

OCI Functions sync timeout defaults to 30 s (max 300 s), detached invocation allows 5 to 3,600 s, memory is 128 to 3,072 MB, and request and response payloads are fixed at 6 MB (https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Functions/Tasks/functionscustomizing.htm).

OCI API Gateway request bodies are limited to 20 MB, HTTP backend read and send timeouts default to 10 s (configurable 1 to 300 s), and method, URI and headers are capped at 8 KB combined (https://docs.cloud.oracle.com/iaas/Content/APIGateway/Reference/apigatewaylimits.htm).
OCI API Gateway allows only 6 MB for a Functions backend, and a larger function response returns 502 (https://docs.oracle.com/iaas/releasenotes/changes/eca7dd82-d5ae-44e5-a574-03c4563e10a7).

Codex automation can use Codex access tokens when the workspace grants permission to create them (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/roles-and-workspace-permissions.md)

A user-owned project API key acts with its owner's access and is meant for personal development (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/api-keys.md)
A project service account and its API key are the documented credential for deployed apps, jobs and CI (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/api-keys.md)

Workload identity federation replaces stored API keys: a workload exchanges a short-lived OIDC JWT, SPIFFE JWT-SVID or X.509 certificate for a short-lived OpenAI access token mapped to a Platform project service account through a 'service account mapping' (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/workload-identity-federation.md)

GitHub Actions OIDC is a documented workload identity provider for the OpenAI API (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/workload-identity-federation/github-actions.md)

ZDR-eligible endpoints are `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/responses` and `/v1/decisions` (with limitations); `/v1/images/*` (specific models); `/v1/embeddings`; `/v1/audio/*`; `/v1/moderations`; `/v1/completions`; `/v1/live/sessions`; and `/v1/realtime` (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/your-data)
