The computer use tool is enabled with `tools: [{type: "computer"}]` and emits `computer_call`, `computer_call_output` and `computer_screenshot` items; examples use `gpt-6.1-sol` (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-computer-use)
For `gpt-6-astra` OpenAI recommends code execution instead of computer use, though `computer` is still supported (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-computer-use)

Computer use environments are self-run (SDK `ComputerToolset`), partners (Browserbase, Browser Use, Daytona, E2B Desktop) or an OpenAI-hosted browser via the Agents API (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-computer-use)

The file search tool is `{"type":"file_search","vector_store_ids":[...]}` with optional `max_num_results` and metadata `filters`; add `include: ["file_search_call.results"]` to return the raw results (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-file-search)
Files must reach status `completed` (indexed) before they are searchable by file search (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-file-search)
The file search rate limit is 500 RPM on Build and 1000 RPM on Launch/Grow (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-file-search)

Set `background: true` on Responses, then poll while the status is `queued` or `in_progress`, or cancel via the cancel endpoint; use `background` with `stream` to resume streams with `starting_after` (a `sequence_number` cursor) (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/background)
ZDR projects still keep background response data on disk for about 10 minutes (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/background)

The Agents API launched in public beta 2026-09-10 and requires the `OpenAI-Beta: agents=v1` header (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents-api/quickstart ; https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/changelog)
The Agents API is at `https://api.openai.com/v1/agents`, for example `POST /v1/agents/sessions` (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents-api/quickstart)

OpenAI describes the Agents API as a managed Codex harness with compaction, multi-agent, programmatic tool calling and MCP, with environments `openai_hosted`, `self_hosted` or `none` (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents)
Computer use was added to the Agents API 2026-09-29 and scheduled automations 2026-10-23 (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/changelog)
Agents API data residency is US-only (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents-api/tools)
The Agents API does not support Zero Data Retention, even with a self-hosted sandbox (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents-api/tools)
`multi_agent.max_concurrent_subagents` caps parallel subagents in the Agents API (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents-api/tools)
The OpenAI-hosted Agents API sandbox is billed at container rates (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents-api/tools)
The Python Agents SDK package is `openai-agents` (`pip install openai-agents`; Python >=3.10) (https://pypi.org/pypi/openai-agents/json)
`openai-agents` is at version 0.24.0 on PyPI as of 2026-11-14 (https://pypi.org/pypi/openai-agents/json)

Python Agents SDK primitives are agents, handoffs and agents-as-tools, guardrails (input/output), sessions (memory), tracing, sandbox agents, MCP tools, realtime agents (`gpt-realtime-2.1`) and voice pipelines (https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/)
The Python Agents SDK uses the Responses API by default (https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/)
`@openai/agents` is at 0.22.0 on npm as of 2026-11-14 and depends on `@openai/agents-core`, `@openai/agents-openai` and `@openai/agents-realtime` (https://registry.npmjs.org/@openai/agents/latest)
The TypeScript Agents SDK realtime entry point is `@openai/agents/realtime` (`RealtimeAgent`, `RealtimeSession`, WebRTC/WebSocket transports) (https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/)
The TypeScript Agents SDK MCP classes are `MCPServerStdio`, `MCPServerSSE` and `MCPServerStreamableHttp` (https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/)

`SandboxAgent` (Python and TS) runs in an isolated workspace defined by a `Manifest`, with the capabilities `Shell`, `Filesystem`, `Skills`, `Memory` and `Compaction` (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents/sandboxes)

Agents SDK sandbox clients include `UnixLocalSandboxClient`, `DockerSandboxClient`, `E2BSandboxClient`, `ModalSandboxClient` and `DaytonaSandboxClient`, plus Blaxel, Cloudflare, Databricks and Vercel (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents/sandboxes)
`SandboxAgent` is part of the Agents SDK in both Python and TypeScript (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents/sandboxes)

Agent Builder (AgentKit) launched at DevDay 2025-10-06 with ChatKit, its deprecation was announced 2026-06-03, and shutdown is 2026-11-30 (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agent-builder ; https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations)
To migrate off Agent Builder, export the workflow code (the 'Code' button) to the Agents SDK (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agent-builder)
ChatGPT Workspace Agents is the other migration path for Agent Builder workflows before the 2026-11-30 shutdown (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agent-builder)

ChatKit, an embeddable chat UI, remains available as of 2026-11-14; Agent Builder-hosted workflows (by workflow ID) are supported only through the transition (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/chatkit)
ChatKit packages are `@openai/chatkit-react`, chatkit-js and chatkit-python (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/chatkit)
The recommended path for new ChatKit work is a self-hosted ChatKit server (Python SDK) backed by any agent service, for example the Agents SDK (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/chatkit)
The Evals platform became read-only for existing users 2026-10-31 and shuts down 2026-11-30 (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/evals ; https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations)

The deprecations page names Promptfoo as the replacement for the Evals platform, and the Evals guide suggests Datasets (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations ; https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/evals)

Fine-tuning is winding down: new users cannot access it, and existing users can create jobs until self-serve job creation ends 2027-01-06 (notice 2026-05-07); fine-tuned models stay usable until their base model is deprecated (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/fine-tuning ; https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations)

Supported fine-tuning methods are SFT, DPO (`gpt-4.1-2025-04-14`, `gpt-4.1-mini-2025-04-14`, `gpt-4.1-nano-2025-04-14`) and vision (`gpt-4o-2024-08-06`) (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/fine-tuning)

The Realtime API went GA 2025-08-28, and the beta interface (`OpenAI-Beta: realtime=v1`) was removed 2026-05-12 (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/realtime ; https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/changelog)

Browsers connect to the Realtime API with WebRTC via `/v1/realtime/calls` using an ephemeral secret from `POST /v1/realtime/client_secrets`, while servers use WebSocket (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/realtime)
The Realtime API supports functions, MCP servers and connectors (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/realtime)
Outbound SIP calling for GPT-Live opened to all organizations 2026-11-02 (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/changelog)
The Decisions API went GA 2026-10-22 with `gpt-6-luna`, after a 2026-10-06 beta; its scope relative to agents was not researched (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/changelog)
The Decisions API has been GA since 2026-10-22, after a beta that began 2026-10-06 (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/changelog)
The Sora/Videos API with `sora-2` and `sora-2-pro` is retired, shut down 2026-09-24 with no one-to-one replacement (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations)

Codex runs in the ChatGPT desktop, mobile and web apps, the Codex CLI, the Codex IDE extension and Codex Cloud; builder tools are the Codex SDK, a GitHub Action and non-interactive mode (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs)
Codex integrations cover GitHub, GitLab (beta), Slack and Linear (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs)

Recommended Codex models are `gpt-6-astra`, `gpt-6.1-sol`, `gpt-6.1-terra` and `gpt-6-luna`, with reasoning efforts Light/Low, Medium, High, Extra High, Max and Ultra (subagents) (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/models)
`gpt-6.1-sol` has a 500,000-token default context in Codex (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/models)
`gpt-6.1-terra` in Codex needs Codex CLI 0.159.0 or later and is not available in the IDE extension (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/models)
GPT-5.5 retires from ChatGPT-sign-in Codex 2026-10-14, a retirement that does not affect API-key sessions (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/models)

Comment `@codex review` on a PR, or enable Automatic review in Codex settings, to get a Codex review; `@codex security review` (research preview) runs a security pass (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/third-party/github)
Codex flags only P0/P1 issues in GitHub, and review rules go in a `## Code Review Rules` section of `AGENTS.md` (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/third-party/github)
Codex GitHub code review runs on GitHub pull requests (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/third-party/github)

The OpenAI REST API base URL is `https://api.openai.com/v1`; `OpenAI-Organization` and `OpenAI-Project` headers select the organization and project (https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/overview)
REST API auth is `Authorization: Bearer <API key or workload-identity access token>` (https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/overview)
A workload-identity access token can be used as the bearer credential on the REST API (https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/overview)
Admin endpoints of the REST API need an Admin API key (https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/overview)

The REST version is v1 (`openai-version: 2020-10-01`); every response carries `x-request-id`, and you can send an optional `X-Client-Request-Id` (ASCII, 512 characters or fewer) (https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/overview)
The Python `openai` package is at 3.51.0 on PyPI (Python >=3.10) and reads `OPENAI_API_KEY` (https://pypi.org/pypi/openai/json ; https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/libraries)
The JS/TS SDK is `openai` on npm (Node, Deno, Bun) (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/libraries)

Official OpenAI SDK packages are Python `openai`, JS/TS `openai` (npm), .NET `OpenAI` (NuGet), Java `com.openai:openai-java`, Go `github.com/openai/openai-go/v3` and Ruby gem `openai`, and SDKs read `OPENAI_API_KEY` (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/libraries)
There is an `openai` CLI installed via `brew install openai/tools/openai` (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/libraries)

The Responses remote MCP tool is declared as `{"type":"mcp","server_label":...,"server_url":...}` with optional `allowed_tools`, `server_description`, `defer_loading` (for tool search), `require_approval` and `authorization`, over Streamable HTTP or HTTP/SSE transports (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-connectors-mcp)

The remote MCP tool's `authorization` field takes an OAuth access token, which OpenAI does not store, so it must be resent on every request (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-connectors-mcp)

`require_approval` takes `"always"`, `"never"` or `{"never":{"tool_names":[...]}}`, and approval is required by default; the model emits `mcp_approval_request` (`mcpr_...`) and you reply with an `mcp_approval_response` input item (`approve`, `approval_request_id`) using `previous_response_id`, each approval covering one call (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-connectors-mcp)
MCP tools are discovered via the `mcp_list_tools` output item, and calls appear as `mcp_call` items (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-connectors-mcp)
Responses MCP rate limits are 1000 RPM on Build and 2000 RPM on Launch/Grow (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-connectors-mcp)
With the remote MCP tool you pay only tokens for tool definitions and calls, with no per-call fee (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-connectors-mcp)

The remote MCP tool is compatible with ZDR and data residency; with `store=true`, data sent to MCP servers is logged for 30 days unless ZDR applies (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-connectors-mcp)
The remote MCP tool also works in Chat Completions (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-connectors-mcp)

`connector_id` connectors were added to Responses 2025-08-21 and are deprecated for models released after 2026-09-01; older models keep support (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-connectors-mcp ; https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/changelog)

Connector IDs are `connector_dropbox`, `connector_gmail`, `connector_googlecalendar`, `connector_googledrive`, `connector_microsoftteams`, `connector_outlookcalendar`, `connector_outlookemail` and `connector_sharepoint` (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-connectors-mcp)
For GitHub, use GitHub's official remote MCP via `server_url` rather than a connector (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-connectors-mcp)
Secure MCP Tunnel connects local or private MCP servers to the Responses `mcp` tool via `tunnel_id` (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-connectors-mcp)
Secure MCP Tunnel was released 2026-05-19 for enterprise customers; a dedicated guide URL was not found (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/changelog)

OpenAI's docs MCP server runs at `https://developers.openai.com/mcp` (Streamable HTTP) and gives read-only search and page content over OpenAI developer docs (https://developers.openai.com/learn/docs-mcp)

Add the OpenAI docs MCP server to Codex with `codex mcp add openaiDeveloperDocs --url https://developers.openai.com/mcp`, or `[mcp_servers.openaiDeveloperDocs] url = "https://developers.openai.com/mcp"` in `~/.codex/config.toml` (https://developers.openai.com/learn/docs-mcp)

In the Agents API, MCP servers go in the agent's `tools` array as `type: "mcp"` with `server_label` and a `transport` object (HTTP with `server_url`) (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents-api/tools)
An API key for the Agents API needs the scopes `api.agents.read`, `api.agents.write` and `api.responses.write` (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents-api/quickstart)
Using the Agents API needs the `api.agents.write` key scope (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents-api/quickstart)
Using the Agents API needs the `api.responses.write` key scope (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents-api/quickstart)

ChatGPT plugins / Apps SDK are built on MCP: a plugin bundles skills and/or an MCP server, with optional UI, and ChatGPT and Codex share one plugin directory (https://developers.openai.com/plugins/quickstart)

Apps SDK docs moved to the 'ChatGPT plugins and Apps SDK' set at `developers.openai.com/plugins`, and `/apps-sdk` now serves Plugins content (https://developers.openai.com/apps-sdk ; https://developers.openai.com/llms.txt)
Plugin submission goes through the ChatGPT Directory review (https://developers.openai.com/plugins/quickstart)

Apps SDK UI is a `ui://` resource with MIME `text/html;profile=mcp-app`, linked from tools via `_meta.ui.resourceUri`; `_meta["openai/outputTemplate"]` is a ChatGPT compatibility alias (https://developers.openai.com/plugins/build/chatgpt-ui)

Apps SDK UI packages are `@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps` and `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`, plus optional `@openai/apps-sdk-ui`; `window.openai` extensions (`requestCheckout`, `requestModal`, `uploadFile`, `setWidgetState`) are optional (https://developers.openai.com/plugins/build/chatgpt-ui)

To add a custom MCP server in ChatGPT, in ChatGPT Plugins select '+' then 'Add custom MCP server', and set the URL and auth (OAuth, none, or mixed); transports are SSE and streaming HTTP (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/developer-mode ; https://developers.openai.com/plugins/quickstart)

ChatGPT custom MCP servers (developer mode) are labeled 'Elevated risk', and tools without the `readOnlyHint` annotation count as write actions, which require confirmation (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/developer-mode)
OAuth registration for ChatGPT custom MCP servers uses static credentials, CIMD or DCR (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/developer-mode)
Webhooks were added to the OpenAI API 2025-06-24, together with the web search tool; event types were not researched (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/changelog)

Since 2026-06-01, OpenAI models such as `us.openai.gpt-6-sol` and `us.openai.gpt-6-luna` in `us-east-1` and GPT-6 Astra in `us-west-2` are on Bedrock Runtime and Mantle with Responses- and Chat Completions-compatible endpoints (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/amazon-bedrock)
`us.openai.gpt-6-luna` is available on Amazon Bedrock in `us-east-1` (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/amazon-bedrock)
GPT-6 Astra is available on Amazon Bedrock in `us-west-2` (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/amazon-bedrock)

Remote MCP, hosted file search, the shell tool, image generation, Programmatic Tool Calling and WebSockets are not available for OpenAI models on Amazon Bedrock (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/amazon-bedrock)

OpenAI models including `gpt-6-astra` (2026-09-03), `gpt-6-luna`, `gpt-6-sol` and `gpt-6.1-sol` are sold by Azure as 'Foundry Models sold by Azure', with Azure deployments, regions and auth (pointer only; covered under the Azure/Foundry platform) (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/models-sold-directly-by-azure)
No A2A protocol support appeared in the OpenAI API docs reviewed (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/llms.txt)
MCP is the cross-vendor tool protocol across Responses, the Agents SDK, the Agents API, ChatGPT and Codex (unverified) (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/llms.txt)

On Windows install Codex CLI with `npm install -g @openai/codex` (`engines.node >=16`; binary `codex`) or `powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "irm https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.ps1 | iex"`; macOS/Linux use `curl -fsSL https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.sh | sh` or `brew install --cask codex` (https://github.com/openai/codex ; https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/windows/windows-sandbox)
The Codex Windows page says `winget` 'should be available', not that it is (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/windows/windows-sandbox)

The latest Codex CLI GitHub release is `rust-v0.169.0` (0.169.0 on npm, published Nov 13), licensed Apache-2.0 (https://github.com/openai/codex/releases/latest ; https://registry.npmjs.org/@openai/codex/latest)

Codex CLI 0.169.0 fixed `codex exec` keeping project config and MCP servers disabled in untrusted directories, and Windows sandbox issues with `cmd.exe`/PowerShell (https://github.com/openai/codex/releases/latest)

`codex login` signs in with ChatGPT (browser flow); `printenv OPENAI_API_KEY | codex login --with-api-key` uses an API key (billed at API rates); `codex login --device-auth` (beta) suits headless machines; `codex login status` and `codex logout` check and clear credentials (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/auth)
`codex login --with-access-token` reads `CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN` and needs admin permission (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/auth)
Without device auth on a headless machine, copy `~/.codex/auth.json` or forward localhost:1455 to sign in to Codex (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/auth)

`cli_auth_credentials_store` is `file` (`auth.json` under `CODEX_HOME`, default `~/.codex`), `keyring`, `auto` or `ephemeral`, and admins can force `forced_login_method` (`chatgpt` or `api`) and `forced_chatgpt_workspace_id` (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/auth)

Under workload identity federation (beta for Codex; `OPENAI_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE`), `codex login` and `codex logout` are rejected (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/auth ; https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/workload-identity-federation)

Codex user config is `~/.codex/config.toml` and project config is `.codex/config.toml`; profiles are `$CODEX_HOME/<name>.config.toml`, selected with `--profile` (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config-file/config-reference)

Project `.codex/config.toml` is loaded only for trusted projects, and project files cannot set `model_provider`, `profiles`, `openai_base_url`, `otel` and similar keys (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config-file/config-reference)

`sandbox_mode` is `read-only`, `workspace-write` or `danger-full-access`; `approval_policy` is `on-request`, `never` or `{granular = {...}}`; `approvals_reviewer` is `user` or `auto_review`; and `[sandbox_workspace_write]` takes `writable_roots` and `network_access` (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config-file/config-reference ; https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/sandboxing)
The Codex `approval_policy` value `untrusted` is no longer supported and `on-failure` is deprecated (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config-file/config-reference)

Codex CLI flags are `--sandbox`/`-s`, `--ask-for-approval`/`-a`, `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox`/`--yolo`, `--approve-for-me`/`--not-so-yolo` (on-request plus workspace-write), `-m`, `-p`, `-c key=value`, `-C`, `--search` and `--oss`; subcommands are `exec`, `login`, `logout`, `mcp`, `app-server`, `sandbox`, `resume`, `cloud`, `apply`, `review` and `features` (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/cli/reference)
`--full-auto` is not documented on the Codex CLI reference page (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/cli/reference)

Codex runs natively in PowerShell with `windows.sandbox` set to `mxc` (recommended; needs Windows 11 24H2 build 26100.9278+ or 25H2), `elevated` (sandbox users and firewall rules) or `unelevated`; WSL2 uses the Linux bubblewrap sandbox (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/windows/windows-sandbox ; https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/sandboxing)
IT can pre-provision the Codex Windows sandbox with `codex sandbox setup --elevated --user <identity> --codex-home <path>` (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/windows/windows-sandbox)

Add MCP servers to Codex with `codex mcp add <name> --env K=V -- <command>` (stdio) or `codex mcp add <name> --url <url>` (Streamable HTTP, OAuth via CIMD/DCR); `codex mcp login <name>` signs in and `codex mcp list` lists servers (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/extend/mcp)

`[mcp_servers.<id>]` keys are `command`, `args`, `env`, `url`, `bearer_token_env_var`, `http_headers`, `auth` (`oauth` or `chatgpt`), `enabled_tools`, `disabled_tools`, `default_tools_approval_mode`, `startup_timeout_sec` (default 10) and `tool_timeout_sec` (default 60) (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config-file/config-reference)

Codex reads global instructions from `~/.codex/AGENTS.override.md` or `AGENTS.md`, then one file per directory from the Git root down to the cwd (override, then `AGENTS.md`, then `project_doc_fallback_filenames`), concatenated top-down (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/agents-md)
AGENTS.md loading caps at `project_doc_max_bytes` (default 32 KiB) (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/agents-md)
The TypeScript Codex SDK is `@openai/codex-sdk` (Node 18+; `new Codex().startThread().run()`, `resumeThread`) (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/codex-sdk)
The Python Codex SDK is `openai-codex` (Python 3.10+, bundles a pinned CLI; `Codex().thread_start().run()`, `AsyncCodex`) (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/codex-sdk)
`codex mcp-server` has been removed, and the app server (`codex app-server`) is the recommended way to build custom Codex clients (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/codex-sdk)

No official OpenAI Terraform provider or IaC tool appeared in the docs reviewed; projects, keys and users are managed through the Admin API with an Admin API key (unverified as complete) (https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/overview)
OpenAI projects, keys and users are managed through the Admin API with an Admin API key (unverified as complete) (https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/overview)

Oracle Fusion Cloud EPM subscriptions are bought by contacting Oracle Sales (web chat or 'Contact sales'), and after the order Oracle emails the designated initial contact with activation and provisioning instructions (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/idcs_buy_epm_cloud.html).

The Oracle Fusion Cloud EPM docs offer a 'Request a Demo' path but describe no self-service trial (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/idcs_buy_epm_cloud.html).

The Cloud EPM hierarchy is cloud account (tenancy) > subscription > environments; the Cloud Account Name is the tenancy, cannot be changed, appears in login URLs, and several subscriptions can be activated into one cloud account (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/idcs_opc_key_concepts.html).
Cloud EPM environments are created in the Oracle Cloud Console (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/idcs_opc_key_concepts.html).

dst: oci iam identity domain administrator role
fact: An identity domain is where Identity Domain Administrators manage Cloud EPM users, and several subscriptions can share one identity domain (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/idcs_opc_key_concepts.html).

A Cloud EPM subscription includes exactly one test and one production environment, designated at creation; more stages (for example dev, test, acceptance, production) require buying another subscription for the extra two environments (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/creating_an_epm_cloud_environment.html).

Creating a Cloud EPM environment needs the OCI Account Administrator role (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/creating_an_epm_cloud_environment.html).

A Cloud EPM environment name becomes part of the URL and cannot be changed; defaults place it in the home region, default compartment and default identity domain, and test and production can sit in different regions, compartments and identity domains (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/creating_an_epm_cloud_environment.html).

Cloud EPM administrator onboarding starts when the Cloud Account Owner (Tenancy Administrator) delegates the administrator role, and the delegate gets an email from oraclecloudadmin_ww@oracle.com titled 'Action Required: Please Activate Your Services' (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmck/epm_cloud_checklist_id_domain_admin.html).

On OCI (Gen 2) the Cloud EPM production URL is https://<instance>-<cloudaccount>.epm.<region>.ocs.oraclecloud.com/epmcloud (for example https://acme-epmidm.epm.us-phoenix-1.ocs.oraclecloud.com/epmcloud) and test adds -test after the instance name (https://acme-test-epmidm.epm.us-phoenix-1.ocs.oraclecloud.com/epmcloud) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsus/1_user_epm_cloud_accessing_sample_urls_gen2.html).

The Cloud Account Name segment of the Cloud EPM OCI (Gen 2) URL was formerly called the Identity Domain Name (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsus/1_user_epm_cloud_accessing_sample_urls_gen2.html).

New Cloud EPM and EDM subscriptions run on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure using OCI IAM ('OCI (Gen 2)' or 'Cloud EPM Gen 2') (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsus/1_user_epm_cloud_accessing_sample_urls.html).

New EDM subscriptions run on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure using OCI IAM (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsus/1_user_epm_cloud_accessing_sample_urls.html).

Oracle Cloud Classic is legacy for Cloud EPM as of 2026-11-14; some customers remain on it and use the separate Classic URL format (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/1_epm_cloud_accessing_sample_urls_classic.html).

On a client engagement an engineer should ask for the test and production environment URLs, an identity domain user with the right application role (normally Service Administrator for automation), an OAuth 2 client ID registered by the Identity Domain Administrator (public client with Device Code and Refresh Token grants) plus the environment's scope, any Network Perimeter IP ranges that must include the runner's egress IP, and the environment's daily maintenance start time (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/epm-cloud/prest/authentication_oath.html).

A Cloud EPM automation user normally needs the Service Administrator application role (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmck/epm_cloud_checklist_id_domain_admin.html).

dst: oci iam identity domain administrator role
fact: The Cloud EPM OAuth 2 client ID is registered by the Identity Domain Administrator as a public client with Device Code and Refresh Token grants (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/epm-cloud/prest/authentication_oath.html).

Any Cloud EPM Network Perimeter IP ranges must include the automation runner's egress IP (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmck/epm_cloud_checklist_id_domain_admin.html).

An engineer starting a Cloud EPM engagement should ask for the environment's daily maintenance start time (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmck/epm_cloud_checklist_id_domain_admin.html).

Cloud EPM identity is OCI IAM identity domains, the successor to Oracle Identity Cloud Service (IDCS); Oracle EPM docs still often say 'Oracle Identity Cloud' or 'IDCS' for this layer (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/idcs_opc_key_concepts.html).

Users, groups, sign-on policies, MFA, SSO federation and OAuth clients for Cloud EPM are managed in the identity domain tied to the environment (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/administrator_roles_defined_at_the_domain_level.html).

Oracle supports Basic Authentication for Cloud EPM REST APIs, but recommends OAuth 2 as more secure (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmai/published_apis_through_external_ai_tools.html).

Oracle supports OAuth 2 for Cloud EPM REST APIs and recommends it over Basic Authentication as more secure (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmai/published_apis_through_external_ai_tools.html).

EPM Automate supports both Basic Authentication and OAuth 2, and Oracle recommends OAuth 2 (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/epm_automate_oauth.html).

Cloud EPM REST Basic Auth uses the Authorization: Basic header with a username of identitydomain.username or just username; the identity domain name appears in the Activity Report and in the URL between epm- (or epm-test-) and the next dot (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/authentication_overview.html).

Oracle's Classic-vs-OCI comparison says Classic used identitydomain.username for Basic Auth while OCI uses the plain username; the page could not be fetched, so this comes from a search snippet and the Narrative Reporting REST guide (unverified) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/idcs_oci_classic_diffs.html).

EPM Automate and EPM Agent use basic authentication, which does not accept SSO credentials, so these users must keep identity domain (traditional) credentials (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/3_sso_config_chap_enable_idm_credentials.html).

The EPM Agent uses basic authentication, which does not accept SSO credentials, so its user must keep identity domain credentials (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/3_sso_config_chap_enable_idm_credentials.html).
Cloud EPM basic authentication does not accept SSO credentials (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/3_sso_config_chap_enable_idm_credentials.html).
epmautomate login is not supported for basic-auth users with MFA (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/epm_auto_login.html).

Cloud EPM REST APIs cannot be run by users configured for Basic Authentication with MFA (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmai/published_apis_through_external_ai_tools.html).
OAuth 2 for Cloud EPM REST is a user-context public client, not client credentials (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/epm-cloud/prest/authentication_oath.html).

dst: oci iam identity domain administrator role
fact: The Identity Domain Administrator registers a 'Mobile Application' (public client) integrated app, adds the EPM resources, sets each EPM base URL (without /epmcloud) as a secondary audience, enables 'Allow token refresh', and selects only the Refresh Token and Device Code grants (not Implicit) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/epm-cloud/prest/authentication_oath.html).

For Cloud EPM REST, other OAuth grants (Authorization Code, Resource Owner Password, Assertion) are allowed only if the token is in an end-user context (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/epm-cloud/prest/authentication_oath.html).

The Cloud EPM OAuth scope is urn:opc:serviceInstanceID=<SERVICE_INSTANCE_ID>urn:opc:resource:consumer::all, with ' offline_access' appended when requesting the first refresh token (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/epm-cloud/prest/authentication_oath.html).

Scopes for more than one EPM environment cannot be requested in one OAuth request, and a token works only for the environment it was issued for (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/epm-cloud/prest/authentication_oath.html).

Bootstrap Cloud EPM OAuth with POST https://idcs-<id>.identity.oraclecloud.com/oauth2/v1/device and response_type=device_code; a human signs in at verification_uri as the user who will invoke the APIs and enters the user_code; POST .../oauth2/v1/token with grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code returns the first refresh token, later calls use grant_type=refresh_token, and the API is called with Authorization: Bearer <access token> (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/epm-cloud/prest/authentication_oath.html).
In the Cloud EPM device-code flow the user_code expires in 300 seconds (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/epm-cloud/prest/authentication_oath.html).

The Cloud EPM OAuth 2 public client uses the device-code flow to get the first refresh token, then rotates refresh tokens (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/epm-cloud/prest/authentication_oath.html).

Cloud EPM OAuth access tokens last 1 hour (sample responses show expires_in: 3600); refresh tokens expire after 7 days and are single use, each refresh returns a new one that must replace the old one, and Oracle advises refreshing at least every 6 days for unattended jobs (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/epm-cloud/prest/authentication_oath.html).
Service Administrators can change Cloud EPM OAuth token expiry on the service's OAuth configuration page (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/epm-cloud/prest/authentication_oath.html).

Scripts that share a Cloud EPM refresh token fail at random with invalid_grant 'The token has already been consumed'; run the device-code bootstrap once per script, and all scripts can share one client_id (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/epm-cloud/prest/authentication_oath.html).

With OAuth, the Cloud EPM access log shows the user name (as with basic auth) but not the client ID or token, so an automation account's actions are attributed to the user who completed the device-code sign-in (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/epm-cloud/prest/authentication_oath.html).

For EPM Automate OAuth, run epmautomate encrypt REFRESH_TOKEN ENCRYPTION_KEY PASSWORD_FILE.epw ClientID=CLIENT_ID, then epmautomate login <ignoredUsername> OAuth2.epw <URL> (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/epm_automate_oauth.html).

With OAuth, the EPM Automate login USERNAME argument is ignored and taken from the token; OAuth is enforced per application, and basic auth still works when OAuth is enabled (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/epm_auto_login.html).

The 25.10 readiness note 'Login EPM Automate Command Documentation Clarification When Using oAuth2 Token' (October 2025) documents that the username is ignored when an OAuth 2 token file is used (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2025/epm-oct25/25oct-epm-wn-f41517.htm).

The EPM Automate commands addUsers, removeUsers, assignRole and unassignRole require basic authentication; all other EPM Automate commands work with OAuth 2.0 (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/epm_auto_login.html).

Cloud EPM REST user and role APIs include Add Users to an Identity Domain (v2, POST /interop/rest/security/v2/users/add) and Assign Role (v1, PUT /interop/rest/security/v1/users with jobtype=ASSIGN_ROLE) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/lcm_add_user_to_identity_domain_v2.html).

The Cloud EPM REST Add Users and Assign Role pages include both -u user:password and Authorization: Bearer cURL samples, unlike the EPM Automate equivalents that require basic auth (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/epm-cloud/prest/lcm_assign_role.html).

epmautomate encrypt PASSWORD|REFRESH_TOKEN KEY PASSWORD_FILE [ClientID=...] [ProxyServerPassword=...] creates an .epw password file; any application role can run it (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/epm_auto_encrypt.html).

EPM Automate password files use the .epw extension and are encrypted with AES/CBC/PKCS5Padding(256); corporate (SSO) credentials cannot be encrypted or used (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/epm_auto_encrypt.html).

The default location of EPM Automate .epw files is ProgramData\Oracle\EPM Automate on Windows and the current directory on Linux (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/epm_auto_encrypt.html).

epmautomate login USERNAME PASSWORD|PASSWORD_FILE URL [IDENTITYDOMAIN] [ProxyServerUserName=...] [ProxyServerPassword=...] [ProxyServerDomain=...] [KeystorePassword=...] signs in; IDENTITYDOMAIN is derived from the URL and ignored (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/epm_auto_login.html).

EPM Automate login supports vanity and API gateway URLs (for example Apigee), and proxy authentication supports Basic, Digest, Kerberos, Negotiate and NTLM but not SOCKS (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/epm_auto_login.html).

To connect Fusion AI Agent Studio to Cloud EPM or EDM REST, an Identity Domain Administrator of the EPM domain creates a confidential application, enables Client Credentials and JWT assertion, changes the client type to Trusted, imports a public certificate (the private key stays in AI Agent Studio), and sets the Token Issuance Policy to Specific with EPM service resources and scopes (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/create_a_confidential_application_for_epm_integration_with_fusion_ai_agent_studio.html).

Oracle Fusion AI Agent Studio integrates with Cloud EPM and EDM REST APIs through a Trusted confidential application in the EPM identity domain (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/create_a_confidential_application_for_epm_integration_with_fusion_ai_agent_studio.html).

Oracle Fusion AI Agent Studio can connect to EDM REST APIs using the same Trusted confidential application pattern as Cloud EPM (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/create_a_confidential_application_for_epm_integration_with_fusion_ai_agent_studio.html).

dst: oci iam identity domain administrator role
fact: The Trusted confidential application for AI Agent Studio is created by an Identity Domain Administrator of the EPM domain, and it is the only documented confidential-client pattern for EPM (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/create_a_confidential_application_for_epm_integration_with_fusion_ai_agent_studio.html).
Cloud EPM human SSO is SAML 2.0 federation in the identity domain (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmck/epm_cloud_checklist_id_domain_admin.html).

Supported SAML 2.0 identity providers for Cloud EPM SSO include Microsoft Entra ID, Oracle Identity Federation, Okta, Ping Identity PingFederate and Shibboleth (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/3_sso_config_chap_idcs_oci_azure.html).

The four Cloud EPM application roles form a hierarchy, Service Administrator > Power User > User > Viewer, in which each higher role inherits the lower roles' access and what each role grants varies by business process (https://docs.oracle.com/cloud/latest/epm-common/CGSAD/4_managing_epm_cloud_users_roles_predefined_roles.htm).
The Cloud EPM Service Administrator role sits above Power User and inherits its access (https://docs.oracle.com/cloud/latest/epm-common/CGSAD/4_managing_epm_cloud_users_roles_predefined_roles.htm).

The Cloud EPM User role sits above Viewer and inherits its access (https://docs.oracle.com/cloud/latest/epm-common/CGSAD/4_managing_epm_cloud_users_roles_predefined_roles.htm).

Non-Service Administrator access in Cloud EPM also depends on each dimension's 'Apply Security' setting, which Oracle recommends enabling (https://docs.oracle.com/cloud/latest/epm-common/CGSAD/4_managing_epm_cloud_users_roles_predefined_roles.htm).

Enterprise Data Management uses only Service Administrator and User; assigning Power User or Viewer in EDM grants no privileges (https://docs.oracle.com/cloud/latest/epm-common/CGSAD/4_managing_epm_cloud_users_roles_predefined_roles.htm).

Private connectivity to Cloud EPM uses an OCI Service Gateway, which needs an OCI IaaS subscription in the same region (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/configuration_vpn.html).

Each Cloud EPM environment reserves one hour a day for patching, the Environment Backup and the 'Artifact Snapshot', and the Activity Report; the default start is between 10:00 p.m. and 1:00 a.m. in the hosting region's local time, and users are logged off with a 15-minute warning (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/6_house_keeping_tasks_daily_maintenance_tasks.html).

During daily maintenance, for Planning, FCCS, Tax Reporting and EPCM, operations such as data and metadata import, Refresh Database and Data Integration run via EPM Automate, REST or the Job Console schedule are blocked (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/6_house_keeping_tasks_daily_maintenance_tasks.html).

For EDM all operations are blocked during the daily maintenance window (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/6_house_keeping_tasks_daily_maintenance_tasks.html).

epmautomate setDailyMaintenanceStartTime "HH:MM [TZ]" sets the daily maintenance start (UTC if no zone); it will not change if maintenance has not run in the last 36 hours (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/epm_auto_set_daily_maint_start.html).

The Cloud EPM daily maintenance start time can be set with PUT /interop/rest/v2/maintenance/setdailymaintenancestarttime (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/lcm_update_maintenance_time_v2.html).

Since April 2024 Oracle randomizes the Cloud EPM daily maintenance start minute when the customer has not set one (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2024/epm-apr24/24apr-epm-wn-f32927.htm).

cloneEnvironment terminates if the source's daily maintenance starts during cloning, so automation should be scheduled clear of both environments' windows (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/epm_auto_clone_environment.html).

New commercial Cloud EPM orders are provisioned to OCI data centers and activated in the region named in the customer's Ordering Document; region names come from search snippets because the location page returned 404 (unverified) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/tsepm/choosing_epm_cloud_data_centers_and_regions.html).

Oracle lists Cloud EPM security features including TLS 1.2/1.3, Transparent Data Encryption and OCI Block Volume encryption, FIPS 140-2 HSM keys, Bring Your Own Key, data masking, Restrict Data Access by Oracle, WAF, API gateway support, virus scan on uploads, Tor blocking, maximum session duration and idle timeout, an immutable and air-gapped backup in a secondary region, access logs and SIEM integration (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/3_info_security_epm_cloud.html).

The Oracle Fusion Cloud EPM: Features with AI book (part G44587-23) has chapters on LLM usage, embedded AI features, EPM Agent Skills and APIs, Fusion AI EPM Assistants, EPM AI in Smart View, and 'Published REST APIs Through External AI Tools' (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmai/toc.htm).

EPM Agent Skills are Oracle-packaged skills for third-party AI agents; each skill bundles instructions, reference material and executable tools (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/about_epm_ai_skills.html).

EPM Agent Skills follow the Agent Skills open standard (agentskills.io), so compatible agents can reuse the same skills (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmai/epm_skills.html).

Download EPM Agent Skills from Settings and Actions > Downloads > 'EPM AI Skills', which saves a zip (package Epm_Agent_Skills / EPM_AGENT_SKILLS); for desktop clients ('ChatGPT/Codex and Claude') extract it into the agent's skills directory, for browser interfaces (ChatGPT, Claude) upload the zip to the skill library, and keep the folder structure intact (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/downloading_and_installing_epm_ai_skills.html).

EPM Agent Skills can be installed in ChatGPT/Codex desktop clients by extracting the zip into the skills directory, or in the ChatGPT browser interface by uploading the zip to the skill library (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/downloading_and_installing_epm_ai_skills.html).

EPM Agent Skills can be installed in the Claude desktop client by extracting the zip into the skills directory, or in the Claude browser interface by uploading the zip to the skill library (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/downloading_and_installing_epm_ai_skills.html).

From the November 2026 (26.11) update, the 'EPM AI Skills' download appears only after a Cloud EPM or Cloud EDM business process has been created in the environment (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-t79512.htm).

In EPM Agent Skills a root router (EPM Skill Routing) sends each request to a domain folder: Auth (Shared Authentication skill), Core (11 infrastructure-administration skills) and Platform (Platform Data Exploration, plus the Strategic Modeling Data Exploration, Scenario Automation and EPS Alternatives skills) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmai/ai_features_at_a_glance_skills_apis.html).

The Core folder of EPM Agent Skills holds 11 infrastructure-administration skills, announced in the 26.11 readiness notes (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-f52308.htm).

The Core AI skills cover access control and identity reports, environment/services/maintenance, Essbase block analysis, Essbase data export, files/Object Storage/SFTP, identity and access management, migration and snapshots, query governor, security administration, simulate concurrent usage, and user activity reports through validated REST operations (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-f52308.htm).

Most state-changing operations in the EPM Core AI skills require explicit user approval, and the skills honor the invoking user's EPM permissions (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-f52308.htm).

The Platform Data Exploration skill, new in 26.11, is part of the Platform folder of EPM Agent Skills and applies to Planning and FreeForm (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-f52295.htm).

The Platform Data Exploration skill reads applications, cubes/plan types, dimensions, members, forms, dashboards and selected Planning values through a packaged 'EPM Client Library' (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-f52295.htm).

Writes are disabled in the Platform Data Exploration skill, but form and dashboard exports can still run configured load rules, which causes server-side effects (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-f52295.htm).

The EPM Core and shared Auth skills need Python 3.10+, and the Planning and Strategic Modeling skills also need Node.js (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/connecting_using_basic_authentication.html).

The documented EPM Agent Skills connection is Basic auth from a private four-line config file (URL, environment name, username, password); accounts that require MFA for Basic REST auth cannot use it (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/connecting_using_basic_authentication.html).

The bootstrap script Auth\scripts\epm_auth.py bootstrap --basic-config-file <file> writes an environments.json session registry under %LOCALAPPDATA%\OracleEPM\ (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/connecting_using_basic_authentication.html).

The EPM Agent Skills package ships 22 OpenAPI-style YAML definitions, for example epm-pbcs-jobs-api.yaml, epm-pbcs-dimensions-api.yaml, epm-pbcs-insights-api.yaml, epm-pbcs-service-connections-api.yaml and strategic-modeling-openapi.yaml (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmai/ai_features_at_a_glance_skills_apis.html).

Oracle says the APIs defined in the EPM Agent Skills YAML files 'will later be documented in the REST APIs guide' (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmai/ai_features_at_a_glance_skills_apis.html).

EPM Assistants are agent teams built in Oracle Fusion AI Agent Studio; agents are imported from JSON and call Cloud EPM REST APIs, scoped to each user's EPM roles (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/downloading_epm_assistants.html).
EPM Assistants call Cloud EPM REST APIs scoped to each user's EPM roles (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/downloading_epm_assistants.html).

Download EPM Assistants as EPM_AI_Agent_Artifacts-<APP>-<SERVICE>.zip from Downloads > 'EPM Assistants', import under AI Agent Studio > Monitoring and Evaluation > Supervisor Agents > Import, test with Play and Debug Play, then Publish (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/import_epm_assistants_into_oracle_fusion_ai_agent_studio.html).

The 'EPM Assistants' download option shows only for EPCM, FreeForm and Planning with AI enabled (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cgsad/downloading_epm_assistants.html).

The EPM Assistants catalog includes Transaction Matching Configuration Assistant (ARCS), PCM Assistant and PCM Calculation Assistant (EPCM), Consolidation Approvals Assistant and Data Retrieval Diagnosis Assistant (FCCS), Narrative Reporting Assistant, Tax Journal Assistant, IPM Insights Assistant, EPM Activity Reports Assistant, and Task Manager Assistants (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmai/ai_features_at_a_glance_fusion_ai.html).
All EPM Assistants are GenAI agents that require AI Agent Studio (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmai/ai_features_at_a_glance_fusion_ai.html).

Several EPM Assistants (IPM Insights, PCM, Configurable Consolidation Rules, Data Retrieval Diagnosis, Transaction Matching Configuration) were announced in the 26.10 and 26.11 readiness notes (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-t79416.htm).
EPM Assistants use the LLMs that AI Agent Studio offers (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmai/llm_availability_and_usage_in_epm.html).

EPM-specific LLM features outside Agent Studio, including the in-product UI features, point to the OCI Generative AI GPT-OSS model documentation (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmai/llm_availability_and_usage_in_epm.html).

The GPT-OSS model referenced by EPM LLM features is documented under OCI Generative AI (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmai/llm_availability_and_usage_in_epm.html).

Cloud EPM environments not on 26.08 or later by the end of January 2027 lose access to Generative AI features (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-t79512.htm).

IPM Insights (anomalies, forecast bias and variances, with GenAI summaries) was first released for Planning in 21.11 (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/planning-budgeting-cloud/pfusu/ai_features_for_planning.html).
Bring Your Own ML (PMML models) is a Planning AI feature first released in 21.11 (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/planning-budgeting-cloud/pfusu/ai_features_for_planning.html).
Predictive Cash Forecasting is a Planning AI feature first released in 24.04 (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/planning-budgeting-cloud/pfusu/ai_features_for_planning.html).
Advanced Predictions (multivariate ML forecasts) is a Planning AI feature first released in 25.08 (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/planning-budgeting-cloud/pfusu/ai_features_for_planning.html).
Reporting Agent (GenAI Q&A over report grids) is a Planning AI feature first released in 26.07 (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/planning-budgeting-cloud/pfusu/ai_features_for_planning.html).
IPM Insights is supported for EPCM, FCCS, FreeForm, Planning and Tax Reporting, and in Smart View (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/planning-budgeting-cloud/pfusu/ai_working_with_ipm.html).

26.11 added IPM Insights Analysis, top insights in dashboards, insights viewed from forms and dashboards, a REST API for Planning insight details, and the IPM-Manage granular role (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-t79416.htm).
The IPM-Manage granular role for IPM Insights was added in 26.11 (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-t79416.htm).

EPM Automate autoPredict and dismissIPMInsights script the Planning predictive features from the CLI (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/epm_automate_command_links_pbcs.html).

Groovy rules can build calc scripts at runtime, validate and cancel saves, and run rules, rulesets and templates synchronously; they run in Planning (including modules, Sales Planning, SWP and Cash Forecasting), EPCM, FCCS, FreeForm and Tax Reporting (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/planning-budgeting-cloud/pfusa/creating_a_groovy_rule_about.html).
Groovy rules need EPM Enterprise Cloud Service, Enterprise PBCS or PBCS Plus One (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/planning-budgeting-cloud/pfusa/creating_a_groovy_rule_about.html).
Groovy rules are not supported in composite forms (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/planning-budgeting-cloud/pfusa/creating_a_groovy_rule_about.html).

In Groovy, getEPMAutomate() returns an EpmAutomate instance that runs EPM Automate commands with no client install (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/epm_auto_groovy_methods.html).

Server-side EPM Automate from Groovy runs every command except downloadFile, upgrade and uploadFile, and recreate, refreshCube, replay, resetService and restructureCube cannot target the environment that is running the script (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/epm_auto_groovy_supported_commands.html).

Server-side Groovy EPM Automate runs in Planning and Planning Modules (EPM Enterprise), EPBCS, PBCS Plus One, FreeForm, EPCM, FCCS (EPM Enterprise), Tax Reporting (EPM Enterprise), SWP and Sales Planning, and a script there can issue commands against any Cloud EPM environment, for example Narrative Reporting (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/cepma/epm_auto_groovy_supported_env.html).

Groovy rules call external or other-EPM REST endpoints through Connections defined in Manage Connections, via the Groovy Connection API (for example operation.application.getConnection("name")); exact method names were not confirmed (unverified) (https://docs.oracle.com/cloud/latest/epm-common/GROOV/).
A future update will block Connection URLs that use IP addresses (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-t79512.htm).

From 26.08, a grid created in Groovy and not closed fails script validation, and if the rule is deployed anyway Job Console shows 'completed with warnings' (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-t79512.htm).

A future update aligns ASO grid suppression for DataGridDefinitionBuilder and the exportdataslice REST API with Form Designer (NON EMPTY MDX when suppressMissingRows is true) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/readiness/epm/2026/epm-nov26/26nov-epm-wn-t79512.htm).

A Data Integration Pipeline runs a series of Data Integration jobs as one process (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/diepm/integrations_pipeline_process.html).

Pipeline job types include Integration, Copy from Object Storage, Copy from SFTP and EPM Platform Job; runtime variables are supported, and non-administrators can be allowed to run Pipelines (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/diepm/integrations_pipeline_process.html).

No EPM-native RAG, vector store, agent memory or evaluation runtime is documented; the external-AI pattern makes the customer responsible for model choice, prompts, security boundaries, auditability and output review (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmai/published_apis_through_external_ai_tools.html).

Agent hosting, monitoring and evaluation for EPM Assistants sit in Oracle Fusion AI Agent Studio, while for EPM Agent Skills they sit in the customer's own agent (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/epmai/published_apis_through_external_ai_tools.html).

The Cloud EPM REST URL pattern is https://<BASE-URL>/<context>/rest/{api_version}/{path}, where <BASE-URL> is the service URL without /epmcloud (for example https://epm-acme.epm.us-phoenix-1.ocs.oraclecloud.com) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/url_structure_overview.html).

Cloud EPM REST context paths are HyperionPlanning (Planning, FCCS, Tax Reporting, EPCM; Enterprise Journal at /HyperionPlanning/rest/ej/, Supplemental Data at /HyperionPlanning/rest/sdm/), interop (Migration/LCM, identity and platform), aif (Data Integration and Data Management), armARCS (Account Reconciliation) and epm (legacy Profitability and Cost Management) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/url_structure_overview.html).

Oracle does not support any Cloud EPM REST endpoint not in the guide, nor any URL containing the path token /internal/, and a bare <BASE-URL> call fails (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/url_structure_overview.html).

The Cloud EPM REST API version is part of the URL and is required; a missing or unsupported version fails and version identifiers are case sensitive (v1 works, V1 does not), yet Data Integration uses V1 (for example /aif/rest/V1/jobs) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/versioning.html).

Planning REST is v3; Migration exposes legacy 11.1.2.3.600 alongside v1 and v2, and GET /interop/rest/ lists versions with lifecycle (active or deprecated) and latest (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/get_rest_api_versions_for_lcm.html).

The REST APIs for Oracle Fusion Cloud EPM guide (part G42939-13) has chapters for Infrastructure, Cloud EPM Platform, Account Reconciliation, EPCM, FCCS, Planning and FreeForm, PCM, Tax Reporting, Identity Domains, Narrative Reporting and EDM REST APIs (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/toc.htm).

Planning jobs are submitted with POST /HyperionPlanning/rest/v3/applications/{app}/jobs and body {"jobType","jobName","parameters"}; the job must already be defined in the application, and record counts and errors come from GET .../jobs/{jobId}/details with offset and limit (default 25) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/execute_a_job.html).

A Planning job response returns jobID and a numeric status: -1 in progress, 0 success, 1 error, 2 cancel pending, 3 cancelled, 4 invalid parameter; poll until status is not -1 (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/retrieve_job_status_details.html).

POST /aif/rest/V1/jobs with jobType INTEGRATION runs a Data Integration integration (recommended over the older DATARULE type), and jobType PIPELINE with jobName set to the Pipeline code and a variables map (for example STARTPERIOD, ENDPERIOD, IMPORTMODE, EXPORTMODE, SEND_MAIL) runs a Pipeline (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/fdmee_run_pipeline.html).

Poll Data Integration jobs with GET /aif/rest/V1/jobs/{jobId} (status codes as for Planning; jobStatus for example SUCCESS, plus logFileName and outputFileName) (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/fdmee_jobstatus_di.html).

Running Pipelines via the Data Integration REST API needs the Service Administrator role (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/fdmee_run_pipeline.html).

Migration (LCM) v2 export is POST /interop/rest/v2/snapshots/export with {"snapshotName":...}, returning status -1 and a 'Job Status' link; poll GET /interop/rest/v2/status/migration/{jobId}, and task details are at .../{jobId}/{taskId}/details?msgtype=error|warn|info (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/lcm_export_v2.html).

fact: Migration v2 snapshot export requires Service Administrator or the Migrations - Administer granular role (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/lcm_export_v2.html).
The Migration v2 export doc says a completed job returns 1 but its example shows 0 (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/lcm_export_v2.html).

Chunked file and snapshot upload (v2): POST /interop/rest/v2/files/upload with {fileName,fileSize} to get a job ID, then PATCH /interop/rest/v2/files/upload/{jobId} with Content-Type: application/octet-stream and a Chunk-Range: <start>-<end> header, then POST .../{jobId}/complete to extract, then poll GET /interop/rest/v2/status/jobs/{jobId} (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/upload_application_snapshot_v2.html).

Migration REST covers list and restore backups (v2), LCM import and export (v2), and rename, upload, download and copy snapshot (v1 and v2); v2 adds artifact categories, incremental category exports, updated-artifact lists, snapshot modification history, selective artifact import, import options and migration status (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/lcm_rest_apis.html).

Copy Snapshot over REST needs the source password encrypted with the EPM Automate encrypt command (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/lcm_rest_apis.html).

Add Users to an Identity Domain comes in v1 (CSV uploaded first with the Upload API) and v2 (JSON payload); it creates accounts only (existing users are untouched), and resetpassword=true sends credential emails (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/enterprise-performance-management-common/prest/lcm_add_user_parent.html).
